news.title: Jelly Roll Risks Trump Backlash by Defending Fat Pig Jab
news.text:
Jelly Roll refused to retreat after drawing criticism for a joke he made about President Donald Trump while guest-hosting Jimmy Kimmel Live! this week, including a jab in which he referred to Trump as a “fat pig.”

The 41-year-old singer addressed the backlash on Tuesday, after some critics accused him of mocking the very audience that has helped fuel his rise, following comments about Trump’s weight during Monday night’s monologue.

Jelly Roll said he found it surprising that those remarks became “the weirdest thing I’ve ever done to stun people,” pointing to his own unlikely life story as a “former felon,” “a drug dealer who has lost 300 pounds,” and someone with “tattoos all over his face.”

The artist, born Jason Bradley DeFord, went on to joke, “What a turn of events: Who would have guessed I’d get in more trouble with the president than Rosie O’Donnell?”

The Save Me singer suggested that anyone occupying the Oval Office should be prepared to absorb a little late-night ridicule.

“Let’s be honest for a second — any U.S. president should be able to handle a few jokes, right?” Jelly Roll said. “They should also be able to handle gas prices, healthcare and the occasional international conflict, but beggars can’t be choosers.”

Our News Outlet has contacted representatives for Jelly Roll seeking additional comment.

The country music star raised eyebrows on Monday after directing punchlines in the president’s direction when speaking about the IndyCar Freedom 250 event in Washington, D.C.

Jelly Roll joked that ‘the president seemed to enjoy the IndyCar race, which was a real switch-up for him because normally he only likes his own race.

‘Trump also drove around the track in his motorcade doing what they call the “lap of honor” – which sounds like a loyalty program at a strip club.’

He then shifted the topic to Trump’s appearance, saying that the Sunday drive marked ‘the only laps Trump’s been doing lately.’

After a montage of clips of Trump alluding to people’s appearances, Jelly Roll said, ‘Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important.

‘It’s crazy, think about this, y’all. In the last few years, I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump – and let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing.’

Jelly Roll on Tuesday said that in the wake of the controversial monologue, he faced pushback from some folks online since he ‘didn’t treat the president with reverence and dignity.’

The entertainer continued, ‘I want to remind y’all that I go by the name Jelly Roll – I don’t even treat myself with reverence and dignity!’

Jelly Roll said he believed many viewers ‘were just surprised that I had any opinions at all.

‘They see a guy that looks like me and assume the only opinion I have is whether I prefer my meth crystal or classic!’

Jelly Roll said jokes about the president come with the territory of the high-profile position, noting the Democrat who Trump prevailed over in the 2024 presidential election.

‘Look, y’all, I get it there’s some people are mad at me for goofing on Trump,’ he said. ‘But if you wanted me to make jokes about Kamala Harris, you should have voted for her!’

He addressed people who suggested a boycott of his material in a tongue-in-cheek manner.

‘So for those who threaten to stop listening to my music based on my comments last night, I just want to say with conviction – go right ahead – cause I’m gonna keep speaking my truth, or my name isn’t Post Malone!’

news.title: Iowa Dems Sand and Turek say no to campaigning with Kamala Harris
news.text:
Iowa's two leading Democratic candidates said they do not want former Vice President Kamala Harris to campaign with them as they run in competitive midterm races this fall.

Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand and U.S. Senate nominee Josh Turek each said this week they would not want Harris, the Democratic Party's 2024 presidential nominee, to campaign on their behalf in Iowa as they seek statewide victories in a Republican-leaning state.

Asked on Aug. 26 whether he would want Harris to campaign for him, Turek gave a one-word answer to reporters: "No." He did not elaborate.

"No thanks," Sand told Politico when asked whether he would want Harris to campaign for him. "Let's move on. We need some new leadership."

Elections: Democrats put a 'bullseye' on Iowa, eager to turn the red state purple

Sand, Iowa's state auditor, went a step further, saying he also does not want Harris to run for president in 2028. He acknowledged that some national Democratic figures, including Harris and former President Joe Biden, would "probably" not help his campaign efforts in Iowa.

At the same time, he pointed to Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, a fellow red-state Democrat who campaigned with him earlier this year in Des Moines.

The comments come as Iowa Democrats debate how to handle the national party's decision to omit Iowa once again from its early voting calendar. It remains unclear whether national Democratic figures will campaign in Iowa ahead of the 2028 presidential election the way they once did when the state's caucuses were first in the nation.

Iowa Democrats seek distance from national party

In the meantime, both Sand and Turek are trying to chart a more moderate course and create some separation with their party, which has been on an electoral losing streak in Iowa.

Registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats by more than 180,000 people in the state, meaning both Democrats will need to win over independent voters and some Republicans to secure a statewide victory in November.

Sand has spoken at length about embracing his "independent mind" during his statewide town hall tour. While remaining a Democrat, he has advocated eliminating partisan primaries to give independent voters a greater voice and has criticized the nation's two-party system.

Even Iowa? Trump's troubles tighten races for Senate, governor

Republicans have argued that Sand is a "wolf in sheep's clothing" who is pretending to be a moderate. They have noted that he supported Biden in 2020 and praised Biden's selection of Harris as his running mate that year.

"Sand can change his rhetoric, but he can't erase his record," Iowa Republican Party spokesperson Jade Cichy said in a statement. "A liberal with better branding is still a liberal."

Turek has highlighted bipartisan credentials, running television ads saying that he voted 700 times with Republicans and would work with Republican President Donald Trump if elected to Congress.

Republicans have also criticized Turek as "too liberal" for Iowa, seeking to cast him as an ally of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.

Rob Sand for president? He shuts down the idea

Sand, who has attracted a national following as he runs for governor, has been floated by some in the national media as a potential 2028 presidential contender himself. The New York Times recently included Sand on its list of politicians who "could make a quick leap" to a national campaign.

Republicans, meanwhile, have criticized Sand as a career politician who they say has been campaigning for his next office since being elected state auditor in 2018.

'Seismic': Texas, Iowa shift to toss-up in tight Senate midterm races

In his interview with Politico, Sand shut down the prospect of a future White House bid.

Asked whether he wanted to run for president one day, he answered: "No." Asked whether he would consider serving as a vice presidential nominee, he again replied: "No."

When the interviewer pressed him on the issue, Sand stood by his answer.

"I told you my answer," Sand said. "You don't have to believe me."

Brianne Pfannenstiel is the chief politics reporter for the Des Moines Register. She writes about campaigns, elections and the Iowa Caucuses. Reach her at bpfann@dmreg.com or 515-284-8244. Follow her on X at @brianneDMR.

Stephen Gruber-Miller is the Capitol bureau chief for the Des Moines Register. He can be reached by email at sgrubermil@registermedia.com, by phone at 515-284-8169 or on X at @sgrubermiller.

news.title: Jill Biden Says Joe Should Be Remembered as a 'Hero' for Dropping Out of 2024 Presidential Race Against Trump
news.text:
Jill Biden hailed her husband, Joe Biden, as a “hero” for making the decision to drop out of the 2024 Presidential Election, RadarOnline.com can reveal. 

During an appearance on Jamie Kern Lima's eponymous podcast, the former first lady denied pushing her husband to abandon his reelection bid, even though Joe reportedly turned to her for advice as Democratic heavyweights called for him to bow out amid questions about his cognitive ability.'I Thought What He Did Was Heroic'"There was so much pressure for Joe to step down and to step aside, and he was losing the support of the Democratic Party. And Joe said to me, you know, 'What do you think, Jill? What do you think I should do?'" she explained to the podcast host.

"And I said, 'No.' I said, 'You make this decision yourself.' I said, 'Whatever decision is made, you have to be able to live with it the rest of your life.' And I said, 'I am not going to weigh in for or against,'" she recalled. 

"I kept true to that. And Joe's advisers came in and they, you know, it was...But Joe, I think, saw the direction that things were going, and he decided to step aside," she continued. "I mean, I thought what he did was heroic. I mean, he gave up everything."Jill Biden Said Joe's Decision 'Was Hard for Him'Jill recalled how Joe had a heavy heart after announcing he was dropping out of the 2024 presidential race.

"I think it was hard for him. But I can remember, you know, going upstairs that night and getting in bed, and I said, 'Joe, how are you doing?' And he grabbed my hand, and he said, 'Jilly, I had no choice.'"

"And, so, he had to step aside. I mean, that's who Joe was," Jill said.

His Vice President, Kamala Harris, was ultimately tapped to replace Joe in the election, but she lost to Donald Trump.Jill Biden Claimed Husband Joe Only Intended to Serve One TermJill also claimed that Joe had originally planned to serve just one term in the White House.

She maintained it was his advisers – buoyed by Democrats' midterm electoral momentum in 2022 – who pushed Biden to seek another four years, repeatedly urging him: “He has to run. He has to run.”

"In the beginning, I mean, Joe did not, was not going to run for two terms. He was only going to run for that one term," Jill revealed to Lima. "And I think people forget that historical context because of all the negative overlay. They forget the true story of what happened."Jill Biden Was Really Proud' of Joe's Sacrifice"I'm hoping that it's revealed in history and that becomes Joe's legacy...that he did it because he believed in, you know, listening to the American people," Jill shared. "I mean, I was really proud. I knew how hard it would be, but he did it."
news.summary: Jill Biden declared that her husband Joe should be remembered as a 'hero' for making the agonizing decision to qui the 2024 presidential race.
news.author: Beth Shilliday

news.title: New Padres Owner Is The Kamala Harris Of Baseball
news.text:
Oh boy … this is going to be entertaining.

Kwanza Jones is both a singer and songwriter, so obviously, she knows how to put on a performance, and she did that with flying colors while being introduced as the new San Diego Padres owner. (RELATED: Commanders Selling Merchandise For ‘Redskins’ Brand They Abandoned — Here’s Why)

Earlier in August, Jones and her husband, Jose E. Feliciano, took the reins of the franchise from John Seidler and his family in a $3.9 billion sale. The two were introduced Monday to the San Diego press, and as you’re about to see, Jones is clearly excited about being the Padres owner.

“We gonna win. We gonna win. We’re going to win, win it all,” yelled Jones while throwing up her arms in the process. “We hope it’s sooner rather than later.”

New Padres owner Kwanza Jones' opening statement: "We are all in. It's not lip service."Her energy is through the roof! pic.twitter.com/LeBSs44899— Talking Friars (@TalkingFriars) August 24, 2026

Give me a replay on that:

Padres new owner Kwanza Jones is confident about the team pic.twitter.com/rXJKeN4FV4— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) August 25, 2026

This totally reminds me of Kamala Harris when she was trying to explain the Russia-Ukraine war.

Roll the tape:

Kamala Harris explains the Ukraine/Russia conflict:“Ukraine is a country in Europe. It exists next to another country called Russia. Russia is a bigger country." pic.twitter.com/QYPLJ02mDy— RNC Research (@RNCResearch) March 1, 2022

Kamala Harris clearly didn’t know what she was talking about, which is why she felt the need to explain the situation like she was speaking with a five-year-old. That’s exactly what Kwanza Jones did.

Instead of addressing roster depth, front-office strategy, or how she plans to navigate a brutal NL West, she gave San Diego the boardroom pep-talk equivalent of a nursery rhyme. And that’s because — and I’m willing to bet a lot of money on this — she doesn’t know a damn thing about baseball.

Kwanza Jones, ladies and gentlemen. The Kamala Harris of the MLB.
news.summary: This is going to be entertaining
news.author: Andrew Powell

news.title: NFL owner's prostitution arrest puts top Dem committee on defense: 'So desperate for cash'
news.text: Jed York, the owner of the San Francisco 49ers, donated thousands of dollars to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) before authorities arrested him on Monday in a trailer park for attempting to solicit prostitution. York was arrested on one charge of "engaging in prostitution" and another for "possessing criminal tools," according to court documents. York reportedly tried to solicit prostitution for $140. 49ERS OWNER JED YORK ARRESTED FOR 'ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION' IN OHIO, PLEADS NO CONTEST TO LESSER CHARGES The engaging in prostitution charge was later downgraded to a "disorderly conduct" charge, according to court filings. York, who grew up in Youngstown, Ohio, was sentenced to one day in a Columbiana County jail for the two charges and paid a $1,285 criminal fine. Despite the unflattering details, it’s unclear if the DCCC plans to give back the $2,500 donation, which was made last June. The group did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Fox News Digital. "We all know that the DCCC is broke, but apparently they’re so desperate for cash they’ll cling to $2,500 through a prostitution scandal," Mike Marinella, a National Republican Congressional Committee spokesperson, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. For his own part, York has a long history of donating to prominent Democrats going back to 2012, including contributions to Kamala Harris’ Senate campaign in 2015, Hillary Clinton’s presidential bid in 2016 and Rep. Ro Khanna's, D-Calif., reelection bid in 2024. KHANNA TORCHES DEMOCRATS FOR RUNNING 'STATUS QUO' CANDIDATES, ADMITS WORKING-CLASS VOTERS WERE ‘SHAFTED’ In total, York has donated over $40,000 to Democratic candidates. York turned heads in 2016 when he made it the San Francisco 49ers’ official stance to oppose gender-consistent bathroom legislation in North Carolina. "The San Francisco 49ers are deeply concerned about North Carolina's recently enacted House Bill 2, which overturned protections for LGBT people and sanctioned discrimination across the state. HB 2 does not reflect the values of our organization, of our country, or the majority of North Carolinians," York said in a statement. York also donated $75,000 to efforts to repeal the bathroom bill. When asked about his political leanings in a 2017 interview over controversies about NFL players protesting the national anthem, York pushed back on characterizations that put him in the camp of far-left figures. "I’m not the most left-wing person in the world. I realize people are trying to sort of paint me as that. That’s not my background politically and how I grew up. But I think a lot of these things are common sense issues. When you actually sit down and talk with people, and you know where people come from, it’s hard not to be sympathetic and empathetic," York told local media. MORE DETAILS ABOUT JED YORK'S ARREST IN A PROSTITUTION STING COME TO LIGHT AND BEGS QUESTIONS ABOUT THE 49ERS His single largest donation was a $5,000 donation to the America 2.0 PAC, a group established by former Rep. Tim Ryan, D-Ohio, in March 2021. York later donated to Ryan on several other occasions, totaling $19,400. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP York did not respond to inquiries about his political donations and whether the DCCC would reimburse his contribution. Khanna also did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's inquiry.
news.summary: Jed York donated $2,500 to the DCCC last June, and the group has not said whether it will return the money following his Ohio prostitution arrest.
news.author: Leo Briceno

news.title: American Medinas: Turning U.S. cities into ‘beachheads’ for Islam
news.text:
Founded by Alexander Hamilton as the first industrial city in America, Paterson, N.J.,  is now home to America’s largest Palestinian community and largest proportion of Muslim residents. Today, New Jersey’s third-largest city is effectively run by its 30,000 Muslims, some of whom say they don’t need to learn English because it’s like living “back home” in an Arab city.

Paterson holds an annual Palestinian flag-raising ceremony, during which residents chant, “Free Free Palestine!” And in 2022, it renamed a five-block stretch of Main Street “Palestine Way.”

In June 2023, Paterson Mayor Andre Sayegh signed a sister city agreement with the mayor of Ramallah, a city in the West Bank and the seat of power of the Palestinian Authority, which officially celebrates the killing of Israelis. And last year during a ceremony kicking off Ramadan, he declared his city the “capital of Palestine in the United States of America” and the “fourth-holiest city” in Islam. “We are 100% halal!” Sayegh gushed, meaning pure and lawful under Islam. The mayor even agreed to hang a sign at the city entrance that reads: “Welcome to Little Palestine.”

Paterson is just one of several American cities – which also includes Hamtramck and Dearborn in Michigan – now controlled by Muslims; followers of Islam also exert outsized influence in some larger cities such as Minneapolis and New York.

To varying degrees, the actions of Muslims in these communities echo those of immigrant groups who came before them – creating thriving communities that can feel more foreign than American, supporting one another to gain office and influence, renaming streets after their own heroes, giving recognition to their own holidays. But critics warn that communities such as Paterson also reflect the different challenges posed by Islam, which is now the nation’s fastest-growing religion.

As is also the case in Western Europe, assimilation is demonstrably rare in U.S. municipalities with heavy concentrations of Muslim migrants. In these areas, large influxes of Muslims from abroad have changed not only the complexion, culture, values and traditions of cities, but also the demographic makeup of city councils, school boards, police departments and courts. Muslim officials, in turn, have changed laws or how existing laws are enforced to conform to the tenets of Islam – an unwelcome trend for many non-Muslims and particularly Jews threatened by their militantly anti-Israel rhetoric and positions.

“Our number one and top priority is to protect and defend our community, it is not to assimilate,” asserted Linda Sarsour, a renowned Palestinian activist who lives in the Paterson area and has helped transform the city.

RCI’s reporting on this phenomenon has found that Muslims often break with U.S. norms on a wide range of fundamental issues – from the separation of church and state and attitudes toward people of different faiths to what constitutes women’s rights and terrorism. As Muslims remake communities in their own images, they are dramatically changing the ever-evolving idea of what it means to be an American.

Not Alexander Hamilton’s Paterson

This is perhaps no more evident than in Paterson, where elected American officials annually raise the Palestinian flag. Several years ago, Paterson’s Muslim-majority city council voted to change existing noise regulations to allow the city’s dozen mosques to blast out the Islamic call to prayer five times a day – from before dawn to after dusk. The move has incensed some non-Muslim neighbors, including one who recently entered a nearby mosque to complain about the noise. “Everybody’s not Muslim here,” the man yelled. “I don’t want to hear that s— every day.”

Paterson’s largest mosque – the Islamic Center of Passaic County – is run by a radical cleric whose brother-in-law was a senior Hamas commander in the West Bank, where he orchestrated a number of suicide bombings against Israelis. Before immigrating to the U.S. from Jordan, this leading Paterson imam, Mohammad Qatanani, served time in an Israeli prison for his own confessed ties to Hamas. Yet he was presented the keys to the city by Paterson’s mayor in 2024.

Until last year, U.S. immigration authorities had sought to deport Qatanani because he hid his criminal record on applications for a green card. But last year, judges appointed by President Obama and President Biden ruled he could stay in the United States. They did so despite testimony showing that he’d called  for a “new intifada,” or violent Palestinian uprising, against Israel in a Times Square rally in 2017.  Hundreds of Israelis were killed during the first and second intifadas, and Qatanani has supported the families of intifada suicide bombers. A decade earlier, he gave a sermon condemning Christians to hell, telling Paterson’s Muslim faithful that “the followers of Jesus” as Lord will burn in the “pits of hellfire.”

The 62-year-old Qatanani, who has also admitted ties to the terror-tied Muslim Brotherhood, oversees satellite mosques in neighboring Clifton and Prospect Park, N.J., as well. His mentor and predecessor at the Islamic Center was its founder Mohammad El-Mezain. Qatanani worked alongside El-Mezain until El-Mezain was convicted of funneling millions of dollars to Hamas in 2008.

Qatanani denies supporting or advocating violence. He declined further comment.

Intensely political, the Palestinian community in Paterson shows up in force at council meetings, voter drives, and election events. Much of the political organizing centers around mosques, where the Israeli-Gazan war is debated and where politicians are groomed – or shunned. After Hamas terrorists slaughtered more than 1,200 Israeli Jews on Oct. 7, 2023, New Jersey’s U.S. representatives, senators and the state’s governor all declared their support for Israel. “That’s right,” Ellison responded, according to a transcript.

“But if you are secure in your donor base, and if you are secure in your power base, you can act the way you want to act,” Omar added.

“Money is freedom,” Ellison said, chuckling.

“We are jumping into the fight with some serious money, serious organizing, and we need you in this fight with us,” Omar asserted. “We are gonna commit to backing you.”

“I’m here to help,” the attorney general replied. “Let’s fight these people … put a stop to it.”

Ellison vowed to convey their complaints to the Minnesota Department of Education. “I’ll call them in my office and demand some explanations,” he said.

A House Oversight Committee investigation concluded that, “Attorney General Ellison knew about fraud in the Child Care Assistance Program as early as spring 2019.”

Nine days after the recorded 2021 meeting, state records show Ellison received $10,000 in donations from some of the convicted fraudsters for his 2022 reelection, though he later quietly returned the gifts – four years later, after their roles in the fraud scheme were revealed, according to Minnesota Campaign Finance Board filings. In early 2022, Ellison got an additional $2,500 from another conspirator in the fraud, records show, but that gift also was returned a year later.

Whistleblowers from the state agencies reported to congressional investigators that “they were told not to say anything about the fraud because they would be called ‘Islamophobic,’” according to the House report.

Critics say Ellison is a cautionary tale about the potential problems with electing Muslims who could be in a position to prosecute fellow Muslims for alleged crimes. The massive fraud case, which could have been stopped earlier, has resulted in a black eye for the Land of 10,000 Lakes. “A once high-trust society devolved into a culture that tolerates the kinds of systemic, large-scale frauds that Somali migrants now perpetrate upon the citizens of Minnesota,” said Steve Cortes, president of the League of American Workers.

Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz counters that the fraudsters represent a small minority of the state’s Muslim population. The 2024 Democratic Party vice presidential nominee has accused critics of “demonizing” a community that has been saddled with what he says is an unfairly negative image.

However, prosecutors say the Somalis arrested are just a fraction of the total number from the community who participated in the conspiracy to shake down welfare agencies. They say participants who could be prosecuted, if authorities had the staff and resources to bring them all to trial, number as many as 320 potential defendants – and they even include leaders of local mosques. One of the most prominent members of the community who participated in the meals programs is the wife of a Minneapolis city councilman who has talked about creating a “Muslim caucus” on the council.

Prosecutors say they have focused on going after the biggest players in the case, some of whom billed millions of dollars to the government falsely claiming they prepared and served several thousand meals a day to Somali children from their small apartment units. Prosecutors say the one scheme may have bilked as much as half a billion dollars from taxpayers.

It’s not the first time Ellison, who did not respond to requests for comment, has been accused of protecting Muslim constituents from law enforcement.

A college-age convert to Islam, Ellison began his political career in 2007 as the first Muslim elected to Congress. He was sworn in on the Quran. Two years later, the young Muslim congressman would defend an extremist local mosque in his home district where more than 20 Somali men had been radicalized for jihad, according to published local reports at the time.

Also in 2009, he held a meeting in Minneapolis urging Somalis to organize themselves into a powerful political and economic coalition to help fend off FBI investigations, the reports said. At the time, the local Somali community was the target of federal investigations into terrorist money laundering. Agents suspected Somali refugees were funneling millions of dollars in fraudulent food stamps through Somali grocery stores into overseas bank accounts used by al-Qaeda.

Ellison joined forces with CAIR to defend the Somali store owners against the allegations, even meeting with the head of the civil-rights unit of the USDA to complain about the agency’s food stamp investigations, according to a confidential CAIR memo obtained by the authors of “Muslim Mafia.”

He also worked with CAIR to help recruit Muslim candidates for office, as well as Muslim staffers to work on Homeland Security and other sensitive congressional committees. Ellison set a goal of electing 15 more Muslim lawmakers and even envisioned forming a Congressional Muslim Caucus. “I want to see many more Muslims serving in Congress,” including as U.S. senators, he said.

Like Ellison, top CAIR officials came of age attending college in Minneapolis around the same time period. CAIR Communications Director Ibrahim Hooper, who roots for “the government of the United States to be Islamic sometime in the future,” and CAIR Executive Director Nihad Awad, who said he was “happy to see” Hamas massacre Jews on Oct. 7, 2023, got their start as Islamic activists in Minneapolis, where they protested Israel.

Awad, CAIR’s co-founder and national director, is so connected to Hamas that the FBI several years ago decided to cut off community outreach to him and CAIR pending further investigation. While running CAIR’s campaign to elect hundreds of Muslims to office, Awad has personally backed such candidates, providing more than $50,000 of his own money to them in state and federal races, according to Federal Election Commission and other records reviewed by RCI. His most recent recorded donation was a $500 gift in April to Hamawy, the al-Qaeda-tied Democrat running for Congress in New Jersey.

Another powerful Minneapolis Muslim leader is Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minneapolis.

A Somali immigrant, she introduced the initial legislation – the Meals Program Act of 2021 – that loosened regulations on federal food programs and enticed her Somali constituents to create a raft of new nonprofits and meals sites to exploit the bonanza of new federal dollars coming to states.

“She sponsored the act that facilitated the Feeding Our Future fraud, and her congressional district served as its epicenter,” said Scott Johnson, a former Minneapolis attorney and Claremont Institute fellow.

Johnson notes that Omar was close friends with Salim Said, who last year was convicted in the Feeding Our Future case on 21 felony counts and attended the recorded December 2021 meeting with Ellison. She filmed a promotional video for the fraudulent meals program run by Said at his now-infamous Safari Restaurant in Minneapolis, which received more than $16 million in fraudulent Federal Child Nutrition Program funds and was one of the biggest food fraud sites conspiring with Feeding Our Future.

It was Omar’s own MEALS Act that allowed for-profit restaurants like Safari to participate for the first time in the food program normally meant for schools. Prosecutors say Said used the millions he pocketed from taxpayers to buy a mansion and several luxury cars. “Yet despite these facts, Omar claims to have known nothing about the fraud,” a skeptical Johnson said.

Rep. Omar’s sister has been linked to some of the main culprits in the fraud ring. State incorporation records show Sahra Noor used the same residential address for her $20 million consulting firm Grit Partners – 17626 Hyacinth Way in Lakeville, Minn. – as another firm, Diversity Childcare Center LLC, used to register its own office. In 2022, Diversity Childcare’s co-owner pleaded guilty to defrauding the child meals program out of $7 million. Noor, whose husband previously worked for the Minnesota Department of Human Services, has not been charged with a crime.

Omar has strenuously denied knowing about the scheme run out of her district. As the number of fraud cases has swelled, Omar has strongly condemned the misuse of funds intended for children’s meals, though Republican investigators on the Hill are seeking to question her under oath about her possible role in the scandal.

Omar’s Somalia homeland consistently ranks as one of the most corrupt countries in the world. Critics warn that importing the values from nations like Somalia is creating an underworld of criminality in host cities across the U.S., in addition to the broader problem of Islamic customs and laws clashing with modern Western social norms.

“We have seen beautiful nations crying out for help. Germany, France, Sweden and other Western countries have opened their doors to the Islamic threat,” warned Krista Shields, who worked as an American Airlines flight attendant on 9/11 and now lobbies Texas legislators to ban Sharia in her state. “America must learn from their mistakes. If we do not fight back now, Sharia will eventually dominate this culture, and the America that millions fought and died for will cease to exist.”

news.title: Tom Tiffany’s Chances of Beating David Crowley to Flip Wisconsin—Polls
news.text: A new Marquette Law School poll showed a close race between Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, a Democrat and Republican Representative Tom Tiffany in the Wisconsin governor’s race, as both parties view the seat as competitive in the 2026 midterms. Wisconsin is one of the most closely divided swing states, so both parties are targeting the governor race after incumbent two-term Governor Tony Evers, a Democrat, announced his retirement. Wisconsin voters have gone back and forth between the parties over recent election cycles, backing President Donald Trump by only about a single point in 2024. Democrats are optimistic about Crowley’s chances, as they believe he will benefit from political headwinds favoring their party. President Donald Trump’s approval rating has slipped to record lows in several polls and threatens to weigh down Republicans in closely divided states. But Republicans still believe the race is competitive, particularly after a divisive Democratic primary that saw Crowley barely eke out a victory against democratic socialist Francesca Hong. Crowley, Tiffany Face Close Race in Wisconsin The new poll gave Crowley a slight advantage among likely voters, showing he has support from 49 percent of Wisconsin voters compared to 44 percent planning to cast their ballots for Tiffany. Seven percent were still undecided about who they would support. Among registered voters, however, the race was tied, with each candidate receiving 44 percent support and 12 percent saying they are undecided. The poll also found that Republicans are more excited about voting. Fifty-five percent of Republican respondents said they are “very enthusiastic” to cast their ballot for their nominee in November, compared to 49 percent of Democrats. “The gap in Democratic enthusiasm may reflect less enthusiasm among supporters of State Rep. Francesca Hong. Among Democratic voters with a favorable opinion of Hong, 52% are very enthusiastic about voting, while 63% of those favorable to Crowley are very enthusiastic,” the pollster wrote in a post on X. It surveyed 891 registered voters in Wisconsin from August 12 to 20, 2026, and had a margin of error of ±4 percentage points. The poll also found that Trump is broadly unpopular among the electorate, reaching a new low of -19 points, with 59 percent disapproving and 40 percent approving among registered voters. That is a new low for Trump’s approval in a Marquette poll, down from a -18 net approval rating in July. Still, Democrats were viewed more negatively in the poll. Unfavorable views of the Democratic Party stood at 60 percent, while unfavorable views of the Republican Party were at 55 percent. On the generic ballot, Democrats led by only 3 points, 48 percent to 45 percent. What Other Polls Show Other polls have also shown a close race between the two candidates. A Platform Communications poll, which surveyed 500 likely voters from August 12 to 13, 2026, showed Crowley up 4 points, 48 percent to 44 percent. It had a margin of error of ±4.4 percentage points. A GBAO poll, which surveyed 800 likely voters from July 30 to August 3 and had a margin of error of ±3.5 percentage points, showed Crowley up 3 points over Tiffany, 47 percent to 44 percent. Meanwhile, a survey released by RMG Research and the Napolitan News Service gave Crowley a 3-point lead, 46 percent to 43 percent. It surveyed 800 registered voters from July 20-24, 2026 and had a margin of error of ±3.5 percentage points. Forecasters expect the race to be close, with the Cook Political Report classifying it as a toss-up. However, Sabato’s Crystal Ball views it as Leans Democratic. On August 12, the forecaster shifted the race to Democrats. Crowley’s victory in the primary over Hong “makes the Democrats modest favorites to start the November campaign,” analysts Kyle Kondik and J. Miles Coleman wrote in the update. “The Wisconsin gubernatorial race moves from Toss-up to Leans Democratic following Crowley’s victory. Crowley will face Rep. Tom Tiffany (R, WI-7), who was only lightly opposed in his own primary. Tiffany is not a moderate: He’s a member of the House Freedom Caucus and has backed President Trump’s bogus claims about the 2020 presidential election, including voting against certifying the 2020 presidential results in Arizona and Pennsylvania,” they wrote. Crowley Leads Prediction Markets Crowley is favored in prediction markets, having a 79 percent chance of winning on Kalshi and an 81 percent chance on Polymarket as of Wednesday afternoon. Prediction markets allow traders to buy and sell contracts tied to political outcomes and current events, aggregating real-money wagers into probability estimates. Prices fluctuate as traders react to polling, fundraising, candidate developments and broader political trends. They measure trader sentiment in the moment but do not always accurately predict the future. Where Crowley and Tiffany Stand on Data Centers The question of AI data centers has become a central issue for this year’s midterms that has crossed traditional partisan lines. In Wisconsin, both Crowley and Tiffany are hoping to make their opponent appear as the pro-data center candidate. The new poll found broad support for a temporary moratorium on data centers among likely voters, with 65 percent supporting and 35 percent opposing such a measure. Earlier in August, Tiffany’s campaign released an attack ad against Crowley for his position on data centers, calling him “Data Center David Crowley,” highlighting his comments that Wisconsin could become a hub for AI and attacking him for supporting a tax incentive for data centers. Crowley, meanwhile, has outlined his own plan on data centers. His campaign website says he would “let communities decide for themselves” whether they want to construct a data center. He also called for guardrails, including requiring 100 percent renewable energy, covering 100 percent of the costs of infrastructure and grid updates, and banning NDAs. Tiffany previously voiced positive views on data centers in February, calling them an “exciting new technology,” but said ratepayers should not be harmed. “It would be unfair to existing manufacturers, for them to pay much higher electricity rates just because a new industry came in. So we’re going to probably have to find a new template if AI and the data centers specifically come into Wisconsin,” he said, according to PBS Wisconsin. On Tiffany’s website, he says he supports ending taxpayer subsidies, giving local communities the final say, preventing “productive farmland” from being used for development, ensuring data centers pay costs they create and banning secret NDAs. Wisconsin Is a Closely Divided State Recent history shows Wisconsin as a closely divided state. In fact, it was the closest state in 2024, giving Trump 49.6 percent of the vote to former Vice President Kamala Harris’ 48.7 percent. In 2020, former President Joe Biden won the state with 49.5 percent of the vote to Trump’s 48.8 percent, flipping the state after Trump won it in 2016. That year, Trump received 47.2 percent of the vote compared to former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton’s 46.5 percent. Trump’s 2016 win ended a decades-long winning streak for Democrats in Wisconsin. Trump was able to flip the state by making inroads with rural, white, working-class voters across the state, many of whom voted for former President Barack Obama in 2008 and 2012. But Democrats’ margins in cities like Madison and Milwaukee have held strong, and they have improved their showings in the suburbs of Milwaukee, keeping the state competitive. Wisconsin last elected a Republican governor in 2014, when former Governor Scott Walker won reelection. He lost reelection to Evers four years later in 2018. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Gabe Whisnant and Gray R. Thomas
news.summary: A new Marquette poll showed a tight race in Wisconsin, as Republicans hope to flip the governorship in November.
news.author: Andrew Stanton

news.title: Jill Biden Calls Joe a Hero. Too Bad the Internet Kept the Receipts.
news.text:
I was today years old when I learned that former President Joe Biden became a hero by finally doing what his party spent weeks begging him to do.

Former first lady Dochtar Jill Biden now says her husband's decision to abandon his 2024 reelection campaign was "heroic." She says Joe "gave up everything" and hopes history remembers his sacrifice.

From the New York Post:

In an interview with The Jamie Kern Lima Show, the former first lady didn’t directly answer whether she was the “Lady McBeth” who pushed Joe Biden to spend four more years in the White House and instead laid the blame at the feet of their long-serving staff.She confirmed that Biden, 83, originally intended to serve only one term as president but claimed, after Republicans had a poor showing in the 2022 midterms, Democratic Party members and his own advisers said he needed to run for re-election.“After the midterms occurred and we won the midterms, and how you know the Democrats were doing so well, and everybody was coming to Joe and to me and saying, ‘He’s got to keep going,’” she said. “His advisors were saying that. People were saying that everywhere, out on the road. He has to run.”Republicans underperformed in the 2022 midterm election, winning a scant majority in the House and failing to take the Senate. Biden, as president and leader of the party, was credited with a successful election....Jill Biden said she hoped the “true story” of what happened in those years would come out in the historical record and said she wants her husband remembered as a “hero.”“People forget that historical context because of all the negative overlay, they forget the true story- of what happened,” she said. “And I’m hoping that it’s revealed in history – and that becomes Joe’s legacy.”She criticized “negative” people who disparaged the Biden family. “People just put whatever twist on it that they want, and mostly it’s negative.”

She also said Democratic advisers and party figures pushed him toward a second term after the party performed better than expected in the 2022 midterms.

There's truth in part of her defense; interviews with Biden's senior staff later showed that many advisers favored another run. They can own their share of that decision. The good doctor doesn't get to hand them her share of the decision because her own words are still sitting there in the public record.

Start with June 27, 2024. Americans watched Joe Biden freeze, stumble, lose his train of thought, get lost on campaign stages, shake hands with invisible people, and struggle through his debate with President Donald Trump.

Nearly two years later, Jill Biden admitted that she was "frightened" watching him. She said she thought, "Oh, my God, he's having a stroke," and that the performance "scared me to death."

From CBS News:

"I was frightened, because I had never ever seen Joe like that before or since. Never," Jill Biden told CBS News Sunday Morning's Rita Braver in an interview airing Sunday on CBS. "I don't know what happened," she said. "As I watched it, I thought, 'Oh, my God, he's having a stroke.' And it scared me to death."Biden was running for a second term when he stumbled through the June 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump, prompting widespread calls for him to drop out of the race. He dropped out a month later, with 107 days to go until the general election, endorsing Vice President Kamala Harris as the Democratic nominee. He became the first sitting president to pull out of a presidential race since President Lyndon B. Johnson stepped aside in March of 1968.

A wife thinking her husband might be suffering a stroke is terrifying. I've had a stroke, and it was the single most terrifying moment in my life, more so for my daughters, who figured out what was happening, did everything right, and acted in my best interests. 

Jill's public reaction afterward makes her current recollection awfully challenging to square with what happens next.

Minutes after helping Joe walk off the stage, Jill stood before supporters and told Joe, "You did such a great job. You answered every question. You knew all the facts."

Supporters chanted "four more years." The doting wife was so concerned over her frail husband's immediate health that the first thing they did after leaving the debate facility was to visit a Waffle House.The next day, she told donors they weren't going to let 90 minutes define his presidency.

If she genuinely believed she had just watched her 81-year-old husband possibly suffer a stroke on national television, "such a great job" was one heck of a postgame assessment.

Her support didn't fade after a weekend of reflection. On July 8, Jill told supporters Joe had made his decision to remain in the race and was "all in." Then added, "I am all in too." 

With four more years, she promised, Joe would "continue to fight for you."

Joe Biden remained in the race until July 21, 24 days after the debate. By then, Democratic support was crumbling, and calls for him to leave had become impossible to ignore.

Jill now says she refused to influence his final decision, recalling Joe taking her hand that night and saying, "Jilly, I had no choice."

The former first lady said that her husband’s choice to run for another term — then to later end his campaign — were both entirely his own, despite rumors that she played a role. Recalling a conversation that took place at their Delaware beach house, Jill said that Joe specifically asked for her opinion.“And I said, ‘No.’ I said, ‘You make this decision yourself.’ I said, ‘Whatever decision is made, you have to be able to live with it the rest of your life.’ And I said, ‘I am not gonna weigh in for or against.’ And I kept true to that,” Jill shared.After he ultimately decided to drop out, Jill said their conversation continued in their bedroom.“I can remember, you know, going upstairs that night and getting in bed. And I said, ‘Joe, you know, how are you doing?’ And he grabbed my hand, and he said, ‘Jilly, I had no choice,’ ” she recalled.As for a reason behind Joe’s decision, Jill said that her husband “saw the direction that things were going,” adding that he was aware of calls within the Democratic Party for him to retire.“I thought what he did was heroic,” she said. “I mean, he gave up everything.”She continued, saying, “It was his decision. I think people just put whatever twist on it that they want, and mostly it’s negative because it’s just human nature.”

Somehow we've traveled from "four more years" and "I am all in too" to a heroic sacrifice made by a man who, in Jill's own telling, believed he had no choice.

Jill Biden is entitled to love her husband; she can defend his presidency, resent the people who forced him out, and hope history treats him kindly.

She can even keep wearing whatever portion of the White House drapery collection followed her home.

What she can't do is rewrite 2024 while the video is still online.

We watched the debate. We watched Jill praise him afterward. We hear "four more years." We heard "all in." We watched Joe stay put until Democrats finally made continued resistance politically untenable.

The Bidens may be finished with the White House, but the internet isn't finished with the Bidens.

And, unfortunately for Jill's latest version of history, it kept the receipts.

news.title: Taxpayer-Funded Socialist Breeding Campuses
news.text:
"In vain are schools, academies, and universities instituted, if loose principles and licentious habits are impressed upon children in their earliest years." —John Adams (1778)

Recently, I published good news about higher education — some colleges and universities are endeavoring to restore campus civility. As the fall academic semester gets underway, some schools are attempting to contain the small cadres of adolescents who are responsible for most campus incivility. How? By endeavoring to instill values in students that, in most cases, parents failed to imbue. And that is a heavy lift.

Too many young people arrive for their freshman year without a solid mooring of values, and consequently are malleable. They can be shaped into whatever form that comports with the dominant campus cultural influence. It is difficult enough for students with solid faith and values roots to withstand the campus peer culture, but those without strong roots are at high risk.

A longtime friend, Brian Beckley, has devoted his career to mentoring high school students so they can pursue their purpose with wisdom, character, and courage once in college. He focuses on fortifying their values so they can join others who stand for what is good and right on college campuses, rather than falling into the leftist abyss.

I asked Brian for his perspective on why students are susceptible.

He responded:

Formation is not optional. Every campus forms students whether it says so out loud or not. The only question is by whom, and toward what. Most eighteen-year-olds arrive with strong feelings and thin convictions. They have been told what to think about a hundred subjects and rarely taught how to think about any of them. They want to be successful and they want to belong, and on a residential campus those two hungers are often fed by the same act: agreeing. A student who has never once articulated why he believes what he believes will borrow a framework from whoever offers one with confidence and community attached. That is not weakness. That is what an unformed soul does.

And that is particularly true of students from broken or dysfunctional families. Effective fathering is a key factor in preparing young people for the challenges they will face outside the home.

Incivility has surged since 2020, mostly in the streets of urban centers, but it has also spilled over onto campuses nationwide.

Fear, hate, and division were amplified over the four years of the Biden/Harris regime, when Joe Biden promised "unity" but called for battle, fomenting factions of hate and division, and baiting violence.

The dominant leftist campus trend this semester is the perennial leftist faculty favorite — the resurrection of failed Marxist ideologies. The latest cycle is being driven by the young Democratic Socialists of America.

Predictably, their agenda is being championed by Leftmedia platforms and showing up in Democrat polls as favorable on socialism. This is particularly the case among students, who have increasingly become the educated ignorant.

Ronald Reagan famously declared of those on the Left, "The trouble with our Liberal friends is not that they're ignorant; it's just that they know so much that isn't so." That may be true of some Demos today, but a lot of undergrad and graduate students have embraced ignorance as a virtue.

Cadres of "useful idiots" are emerging from the Gen Y and Gen Z age groups. I labeled these cadres "Gen N: The Narcissist Generation," a malignancy of young narcissists. They will form the core of the Left's "Woke 2.0" ranks.

It is no mystery why college students are persuaded down dark paths. One reason is that an overwhelming number of faculty embrace leftist views. The American Enterprise Institute’s Roger Pielke has thoroughly documented the political sentiments of partisan professors, noting:

Faculty in U.S. universities overwhelmingly hold views on the political left. ... The lack of diversity among professors is problematic for both education and research, ostensibly the overriding purposes of universities. A more insidious and fundamental issue is that some extremely partisan faculty (and administrators) have commandeered university departments, centers, institutes — even entire campuses —and repurposed them for political advocacy.

The journal Inside Higher Ed found that almost 80% of faculty nationwide supported Kamala Harris in 2024, with only 7% supporting Donald Trump — but it also noted that "almost no respondents said they plan to tell students which party or candidate to vote for." Newsflash: They didn't have to!

And this bias is even more pronounced in the Ivy League. A study of 1,099 Yale faculty donations in 2025 found that not a single recipient was a Republican.

This month, the American Association of University Professors, which claims a membership of 57,000 of the 190,000 university professors nationwide, broke its century-old practice of not endorsing candidates. It did not even endorse Barack Obama, but it has decided to make its first-ever national political endorsement by backing Michigan's Islamist Democratic Socialist Senate nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

El-Sayed is the most anti-American individual to ever seek the Senate. But I am sure those AAUP profs will not tell their students how to vote...

Educational institutions are full of "scholars" who promote socialism. Fox News analyst Brian Brenberg notes: "College is one of the only places where bad ideas can keep living because they never get tested against reality. So, professors, they study these things, they love the ideas of what socialism promises. They never have to do them in real life. They spend their academic career filling kids' heads with these ideas. Kids who gotta go out in the real world."

But it's more than just indoctrination by faculty.

In a Wall Street Journal column, "How Colleges Produce Socialists," business professor Kimberlee Josephson notes: "The usual assumption is that professors are indoctrinating students, but that’s too simple. The campus itself is a powerful factor."

Over the past several decades, the college campus has morphed into a comprehensive residential and lifestyle provider. ... This transformation has been especially pronounced at America’s wealthiest and most selective colleges and universities. At elite institutions, students enter a nearly self-contained community. They ride campus buses without paying a fare. They enter expansive recreation centers without a membership card. They attend concerts, meet career coaches, reserve study rooms, download software, join student organizations, and participate in countless campus activities without ever reaching for a wallet. None of these services are free. Their costs are embedded in tuition and fees, endowment income, donor support and government funding. Yet, because students rarely confront a price at the point of use, they experience consumption without consequence or even comparison.

She concludes: "The irony is striking. America’s leading universities devote enormous effort to preparing graduates for participation in a dynamic market economy, yet daily campus life is one of the least market-oriented environments in the world. ... The most influential economics lesson many students receive may come from the institutional design of the university."

As Brian Beckley sums it up, "A young person whose first taste of adult life is abundant consumption with invisible production has been taught an economics lesson no syllabus assigned."

As a result of the campus indoctrination issues, an interesting trend has emerged since 2020.

Universities in the Southeast with more conservative cultures have experienced a massive surge in freshman applications from Northeastern states and other parts of the country — what is being called "self-sorting" by political views. The New York Times laments that "because of polarization and self-sorting, the college experience has become more political than ever," and not in the political direction Democrats and the media would like.

To be clear, the current tenor of campus protests is a mere shadow of the violent protests during the 1960s and '70s, and efforts to restore civility now are critical to avoid a resurgence of the violence from that era.

Bottom line: Solid faith and values instilled in young people are the antidote to leftist indoctrination on campus.

news.title: Nate Silver Thinks Texas Could Flip. Here’s Why Republicans Should Stay Calm.
news.text:
So is he right?

Talarico is challenging Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton (R-Texas) for the Senate seat, with Democrats hoping a win helps flip the Senate in 2026. Nate Silver's FLIPR model now rates the race as "leans Democratic" or a toss-up, a striking shift for deep-red Texas. Talarico had raised almost $69 million as of the FEC's June 2026 deadline, even as his own ads claim he's falling short of his fundraising goals. RealClearPolling had him up 1.7% over Paxton.

Silver used to be the golden boy of political forecasting, so when his model moves, people notice. But call me skeptical.

Why? His recent record is spotty. 

In 2016, his model gave Hillary Clinton a 71% chance of winning and predicted she'd carry Florida, Michigan, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. She lost all five. Things haven’t exactly gotten much better for him over the years. His battleground error ran about four points in 2020. In 2024, his model gave Kamala Harris a slight edge, and he called the race a coin flip. Kamala went on to lose every swing state.

None of that screams reliable.

There are factors at play here as well. As we previously reported, pollster Patrick Ruffini researched polling patterns and found that Senate polling in red states has overstated Democratic support every summer for the last four cycles. So, if you assume the pattern holds in 2026, Silver’s model is based on data that likely inflates Talarico’s support.

Texas polling has been unreliable in Texas before. In 2024, Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) beat Democrat Colin Allred by nine points, double the RCP average's margin. Talarico is no moderate.

Recommended: Graham Platner May Be Trying to Shake Up Maine's Senate Race Behind the Scenes

I’m no polling expert, so what really makes me question Talarico’s ability to pull off a victory in Texas isn’t so much what the polls say, don’t say, or how off they may be, but rather just understanding what kind of state Texas is and what kind of candidate Talarico is.

The last Democrat to win a Texas Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. Texas hasn't elected a Democrat statewide since 1994. Donald Trump won Texas by 14 points in 2024, and it's exceedingly rare for a president who carries a state by double digits to see it flip to a non-incumbent from the other party two years later; from what I’ve been able to find, it’s happened only three times since the 1990s, and typically involves moderate candidates with crossover appeal.

Where is Talarico’s crossover appeal? His positions on religion, transgenderism, and women's sports are far out of step with mainstream Texas voters, a factor that should hurt him as the race heats up.

So no, this isn't the moment for Republicans to panic. Silver's model may be flashing signs of concern, but I wouldn’t take it as gospel. Every summer brings a mirage like this one, and every fall it evaporates.

news.title: Why Trump felt the need to KNEECAP Oklahoma's Republican AG
news.text:
President Donald Trump threw his weight behind Mike Mazzei in Oklahoma's GOP gubernatorial primary runoff, which evidently helped the former state senator over the finish line on Tuesday.

While the president's backing certainly had much to do with the politics and character of Mazzei — whom former Oklahoma U.S. Sen. Markwayne Mullin, now Trump's Department of Homeland Security secretary, and Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders had also endorsed — it appears to have also had much to do with the politics and character of Mazzei's unsuccessful opponent, Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond.

'This is what Drummond, and his equally Liberal wife, Wendy, supported at levels that are shameful.'

A week ahead of the runoff primary election, the president explained his issues with Drummond. Trump called him a "FAKE Republican, who donated to SLEEPY Joe Biden, and the totally corrupt and anti-American 'Lincoln Project,' which is now in shambles because of their views on Open Borders, Men playing in Women’s Sports, and Transgender Mutilization of your Children."

Federal Election Commission records show that a $1,000 donation was made in Drummond's name to the Biden for President committee in August 2020. Matthew Parker, the chairman of the state AG's doomed gubernatorial campaign, claimed, however, that the contribution was made by Drummond's wife, Wendy, the Frontier reported.

According to a Sept. 4, 2020, email obtained by the Frontier, Wendy Drummond requested that ActBlue change the name on the contribution to hers. The Biden committee reportedly refunded Gentner Drummond the full amount four days later.

In a previous statement to Blaze News, Parker said: "The Biden contribution lie has been debunked repeatedly. Gentner Drummond gave nothing to Joe Biden. In fact, Gentner was one of President Trump’s largest Oklahoma donors. Repeating a lie doesn’t make it true."

RELATED: GOP Oklahoma governor candidate wants to stop voter ID and invites Dems to help — campaign says the clips are deceptive

 Win McNamee/Getty Images

In September 2020, Wendy Drummond also donated $1,000 to the Lincoln Project, a group founded by George Conway, Steve Schmidt, John Weaver, and Rick Wilson to "stem the damage [Trump] and his followers are doing to the rule of law, the Constitution, and the American character."

The Lincoln Project staged a white supremacy rally, bankrolled efforts to torpedo Trump-aligned Republicans, and churned out pro-Kamala Harris content, including the "Be a Man, Vote for a Woman" ad. The group largely imploded after its co-founder John Weaver was accused by over 20 young men of predatory sexual misconduct.

Trump noted further in his takedown, "This is what Drummond, and his equally Liberal wife, Wendy, supported at levels that are shameful and, frankly, that makes them both Radical Left Dumocrats."

In addition to faulting Drummond for blocking a proposed aluminum plant in Oklahoma, Trump noted that Drummond "stated publicly he had 'no opinion'" on Trump's 2021 impeachment and that Drummond "even SUED to BLOCK a religious based charter school strongly supported by my Administration — Very troubling for Educational Freedom, and an outright attack on Christianity!"

While it was clear from the post that Trump already had ample cause to champion Mazzei over Drummond in the Republican runoff, audio recording of Drummond's commentary about voter ID may have helped convince those still uncertain about his real political outlook.

In the audio recording, Drummond can be heard calling on Democrats and independents to help kill a pair of ballot questions that showed up on the Aug. 25 ballot. One of those questions would "require proof of identity to vote in any election authorized by law and conducted by a county election board or the State Election Board."

"We have to vote 'no' on both state questions," Drummond said in the recording.

Parker previously told Blaze News that the clips had been "stripped of context and selectively edited to manufacture a false narrative."

Drummond noted on Tuesday that the runoff "election comes down to trust," but evidently, not enough trust was on his side. With 99% of the ballots counted, Mazzei had 50.3% of the vote and Drummond had 49.7%.

The voter ID question also passed.

news.title: Democrats Panned for Outspoken Pro-Israel Pick for Key House Middle East Post
news.text:
Progressive and pro-Palestine critics on Tuesday accused House Democratic leaders of ignoring the majority of party voters who oppose U.S. military aid to Israel by appointing one of the most pro-Israel members of Congress as the top Democrat on a key Mideast subcommittee.

Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY), the leading Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, announced the appointment of Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.) as ranking member of the Middle East and North Africa Subcommittee. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-Fla.) was assigned to the Oversight and Intelligence Subcommittee, Mark Pocan (D-Wis.) joined the Africa Subcommittee, and Wesley Bell (D-Mo.) was named to the Western Hemisphere Subcommittee.

Moskowitz thanked Meeks and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) on social media “for this important responsibility” and, in a separate post, vowed to “work to strengthen America’s relationships with Israel and our Gulf allies, expand regional peace, advance American diplomacy, and ensure our foreign policy is grounded in strength, security, and reality.”

During his two terms in Congress, Moskowitz — who last week survived a primary challenge by pro-Palestine progressive Oliver Larkin — has repeatedly argued against conditioning armed aid to apartheid Israel on compliance with international law or protection of Palestinian civilians amid the ongoing genocide in Gaza and Israel’s illegal occupation, colonization, and ethnic cleansing in the West Bank.

Moskowitz was one of only 12 Democrats who voted for a 2023 Republican aid package to Israel — which receives billions of dollars in annual U.S. funding — as the Israeli military killed thousands of Palestinian civilians in Gaza following the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack.

Critics argued that placing one of Congress’ most outspoken supporters of Israel in a key Middle East policy position shows that Democratic leadership remains badly out of step with its own voters, a majority of whom concur with a United Nations commission of inquiry, human rights groups, scholars, and around 20 national governments who say Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Moskowitz denies the Gaza genocide, has conflated criticism of Israeli crimes with hatred of Jews, and was denounced by House progressives including Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), the only Palestinian American in Congress, for authoring an amendment to ban US officials from using State Department funds to cite official Gaza casualty figures — which now include more than 250,000 Palestinians killed, wounded, or missing during Israel’s onslaught.

Meeks’ appointments come at a time when 3 in 4 Democratic voters oppose U.S. aid to Israel — up from just 45% three years ago — and after the issue was a factor in former Vice President Kamala Harris’ defeat by President Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election.

In response to Moskowitz’s appointment, the progressive organizing group Demand Progress issued a statement noting that the congressman “has consistently opposed placing conditions on military aid to Israel, repeatedly voted against the majority of House Democrats to sanction International Criminal Court officials, and earlier this year said he would oppose an Iran war powers resolution.”

Demand Progress senior policy adviser Cavan Kharrazian said:

By making a hard-line Israel supporter their point person on Middle East policy, House Democratic leaders are doubling down on a failed approach to Israel that shows contempt for the clear and growing majority of Democratic voters who want to stop cutting blank checks for the Israeli government. Donald Trump’s ongoing wars in the Middle East and his commitment to keeping the U.S. joined at the hip to Israel are wildly unpopular and have been a disaster for the nation. Elevating someone who consistently sides with Trump in support of Israel, and who has a long record as an Iran hawk, represents clear political malpractice on behalf of House Democratic leaders.

Palestine defenders and Democrats concerned about the possible fallout of elevating an Israel hawk to a top subcommittee post as the party seeks to win back control of Congress in November’s midterm elections bdenounced the appointment of Moskowitz.

ReThinking Foreign Policy president Mitchell Plitnick called Meeks’ move “very bad news.”

“Moskowitz is a completely inappropriate choice, given how wildly out of step he is with Democratic voters on Mideast issues,” he said on X. “It’s yet another indication of why it is so desperately important that Democratic ‘leaders’ like Hakeem Jeffries and Gregory Meeks be replaced as soon as possible.”

Erik Sperling, executive director at Just Foreign Policy, called the decision to appoint Moskowitz “shocking.”

“Meeks and Jeffries are apparently intending to signal that the anti-war and pro-Palestinian movements are unwelcome in the [Democratic] Party?”

Writer Wajahat Ali asked on X, “How much damage will Democratic leaders cause to their own brand and party for AIPAC money?”

Ali was referring to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, whose campaign contributions have been a deciding factor in electing pro-Israel candidates to Congress and defeating those who advocate for Palestinian rights. So far, AIPAC has poured more than $100 million into the 2026 midterm elections — including around $30 million against Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed.

According to the watchdog group Track AIPAC, Moskowitz has received $833,288 in campaign contributions from the Israel lobby over the course of his career, Wasserman Schultz has taken $1,542,327, and Bell — who ousted former Rep. Cori Bush (D-Mo.) — a staggering $18,126,578. Pocan, a pro-Palestine progressive, rejects AIPAC funding.

As for Jeffries and Meeks, Track AIPAC reports the former has taken $1,495,709 and the latter $986,946 in campaign contributions from the Israel lobby.

The local grassroots group NY Dumps AIPAC lamented Meeks’ appointment of what it called “one of the most Islamophobic genocide cheerleaders in Congress to be the top House Dem overseeing Middle Eastern foreign policy.”

“In doing so, Meeks is compromising world peace for the sake of AIPAC,” the group said.

Some observers, including Zeteo News reporter Prem Thakker, noted that Tuesday’s moves followed Jeffries’ recent secret meeting with Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and special envoy for peace missions.

Responding to Moskowitz’s promotion, Matt Duss, executive vice president at the Center for International Policy and a former foreign policy adviser to U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), highlighted polling published Monday by the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project showing that “Democrats in the first six states to vote in the 2028 presidential primary overwhelmingly demand sanctions and a total weapons embargo against Israel.”

“At what point,” asked Duss, “can Democratic voters finally have foreign policy committee leadership that actually represents the party’s anti-war majority instead of its small and thankfully dwindling hawkish minority?”
news.summary: Observers note that Jared Moskowitz’s appointment follows Hakeem Jeffries’s recent secret meeting with Jared Kushner.

news.title: Rob Sand says Kamala Harris shouldn’t run for president in 2028
news.text:
Sand is one of the first high-profile Democrats to say publicly that Harris should not run again in 2028. The vice president has signaled she is weighing another run after her unsuccessful 107-day campaign against President Donald Trump.

Harris remains the front-runner among 2028 Democratic hopefuls, according to several polls. Very few Democrats have publicly and full-throatedly said it is time for the party to move on from Harris, in an effort not to anger supportive black voters’ sizable impact in the presidential primary.

But Democrats in Iowa, who are hoping to snatch back control of an open Senate seat and the governorship, are publicly urging Harris to stay out of the state this election cycle.

“No thanks,” Sand said when asked about Harris or former President Joe Biden campaigning for him in Iowa. “Let’s move on. We need some new leadership.”

Campaign spokespeople for Sand and Iowa Democratic Senate nominee Josh Turek previously told the Washington Examiner they do not want an endorsement from Harris, nor do they want her to appear at any campaign rallies this cycle.

ROB SAND AND JOSH TUREK DON’T WANT KAMALA HARRIS TO CAMPAIGN FOR THEM IN IOWA

Iowa Democrats are hoping to reverse the state’s turn to the GOP under Trump’s leadership this election cycle. They received a boost last week when the Cook Political Report moved the Iowa gubernatorial race from a toss-up to leans Democratic and changed Iowa’s Senate race from leans Republican to a toss-up.

Sand touted his past registration as an independent, but in 2018, he was boosted by Harris’s support for his campaign for Iowa state auditor.

news.title: Trump Pushed Black Farmers Away From the Table. John Boyd is fighting back.
news.text:
John Boyd Jr. has spent three decades getting Black farmers a seat at the table in Washington. Under the Trump administration, he says, the invitations stopped coming and Black farmers are suffering.

“It’s like night and day based on the treatment that we receive from this administration,” the founder and president of the National Black Farmers Association told The Root. “This president clearly says he doesn’t want us.”

In an exclusive interview, Boyd said the administration’s policies — from canceled agricultural grants to a push to bring more foreign beef into the U.S. market — are pushing farmers who were already struggling closer to losing their land. And he’s just as frustrated with the silence coming from Black America.

RELATED: Black Leaders Push Back as Supreme Court Clears Path for Trump’s Mail-Voting Order

Boyd said previous administrations, both Democratic and Republican, gave him access to policymakers and opportunities to advocate for Black farmers, including billion-dollar funding from the Clinton, Obama and Biden administrations. Under Trump, Boyd says, he has instead been excluded from White House events and agricultural discussions.

“I led the way on all of those efforts,” Boyd said of the billion-dollar settlements. “And this administration came in and said, ‘Hey, Boyd, we can’t– we don’t even want you at the table.’”

For the veteran farmer, the lack of access is more than symbolic. He says the administration’s agricultural policies are creating real financial consequences for farmers already struggling to stay on their land.

The latest fight centers on beef. The administration has moved to increase foreign beef imports in an effort to bring down prices for consumers, according to the Guardian. Boyd argues that the policy will put additional pressure on American cattle producers by driving down what farmers receive for their livestock.

The consequences could extend well beyond Black farmers. Boyd noted that white farmers also have significant amounts of cattle and potentially more to lose financially.

“It’s the beginning of something different from the agricultural sector in this country,” he said. “This president has ruined the agricultural sector in this country for many years to come. The grain markets are gone, and now he wants to give the beef counter market to his friends.”

But Boyd’s frustration is not limited to the White House. The 60-year-old activist is calling out the Congressional Black Caucus, prominent activists, athletes, entertainers and wealthy Black Americans for remaining largely silent as Black farmers face financial pressure.

“We got athletes, boxers, tennis players, wealthy businessmen,” Boyd said. “Nobody’s picked up the phone and say, ‘Hey, Boyd, what can I do to help?’”

He says the help Black farmers need is not another symbolic gesture. Boyd says hundreds of farmers are facing foreclosure and he wants people with resources and influence to help individual farmers stay on their land.

“That’s the kind of help I need right now,” he said. Boyd also rejects the idea that Black farmers supported Trump. He, like many of his peers, backed former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 and has spent years advocating for Black farmers regardless of party.

“We don’t want Trump. I don’t want him now. He doesn’t want me,” Boyd said.

His message to Black Americans is direct: learn the history, organize and vote.

“We have to vote our way out of this and there needs to be a sense of urgency,” Boyd said. For him, the fight is bigger than Trump. It is about whether Black farmers will have a voice in the future of American agriculture — and whether the people who have the power to help them will finally use it.

“We’re gonna survive Trump,” Boyd said. “We survived Jim Crow, we survived slavery and sharecropping… But the only way to get through it is to work together, in unity.”
news.summary:
Boyd is calling out the Congressional Black Caucus and prominent Black voices for staying quiet as farmers face mounting pressure from the Trump administration.
