 Jim Dyson / Getty Images

“She was a very clever business woman who understood the value of her music and, most importantly, the effect that she had on the people of the world,” he continued. “There was no greater honour for me than to have her sing my song Let It Be and, even though I only made a small contribution to it, I am so honoured that she did it. I am so proud to have known her and admire her unique talents. Thanks Dolly for the beautiful music you gave me and the whole world. We will always love you, god bless and rest in peace. You were the best.”

 Posting a photo of himself and Dolly on stage, Elton John wrote, “Shocked and devastated to hear of Dolly’s passing. A giant of an artist - unique and irreplaceable, with the kindest heart.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @eltonjohn / Michael Loccisano / FilmMagic for Country Music Association

 Keith Urban shared an Instagram Story that read, “heartbroken today…Dolly Parton💔 honestly…I have no words right now.”

 @keithurban / Via Instagram: @https://www.instagram.com/keithurban/?hl=en

 In a statement shared with NBC News, per TODAY, singer Patti LaBelle said, “I am deeply saddened by the loss of my dear friend who was loved by all. Dolly’s artistry, brilliance, and extraordinary life inspired so many people, including me. Her light will forever shine! I send my deepest condolences to all of her loved ones and fans all over the world!”

 Erika Goldring / Getty Images

 Country star Reba McEntire wrote on Instagram, “Well, I just got the news that my buddy Dolly passed onto the higher and greater side. Dolly, thank you for all the wonderful things you did for us here on earth. Your love, your music and you gave so much with your huge huge heart. There will never ever be another you.”

 Kevin Winter / Getty Images

“We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang. Thank you, Lord, for Dolly. She’s gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her,” Reba said. “I’ll never forget the first time I met you and I’ll never forget our last conversation. I hold it with love in my heart.”

 Darlene Love said, “I’m truly heartbroken. This one really hurts. 💔 Dolly Parton was one of a kind — an extraordinary talent, a beautiful soul, and a woman whose music, kindness and spirit touched generations. Her light will continue to shine through the incredible legacy she leaves behind. Rest in peace, Dolly. You will be deeply missed and forever loved. ❤️🙏🏽”

 Jason Mendez / Getty Images

 Dionne Warwick wrote, “I will certainly miss her laugher, jokes and her being. Rest well and in total peace my friend. My heart is heavy.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @dionnewarwick / Kind Music Group / Via youtube.com

 Seth MacFarlane wrote, “The news of Dolly Parton’s passing is devastating. I had the extraordinary experience of working with her on The Orville, and it was a joy to discover that she really was exactly the person we all hoped she was. Her kindness, generosity, and authenticity were evident from moment one, and the benign yet assured command she maintained over her empire was obvious from the genuine love and trust you could see from everyone who worked for her. The world is a dimmer place today without her.”

 Rich Polk / Getty Images

 Mick Jagger said, “What a wonderful songwriter and singer Dolly was. She brought so many people together, we will all miss her so much.”

 Allan Tannenbaum / Getty Images

 The Jacksons shared a statement that read, “We are deeply saddened by the passing of the incomparable Dolly Parton. Dolly was a true trailblazer. Through her extraordinary talent, kindness and generosity, she opened doors and inspired generations around the world…Thank you, Dolly, for the music, the joy and the light you shared with us all. May you rest peacefully in the loving arms of the Lord, reunited with your husband Carl and the many loved ones who made their journey to Heaven before you.”

 Sebastian Reuter / Getty Images

“Our prayers are with Dolly’s family, friends and everyone whose life she touched. Rest in peace, Dolly. Your beautiful spirit and remarkable legacy will live on forever. 🙏🏾🕊️,” they added.

 Khloé Kardashian, who featured Dolly as a guest on her Khloé in Wonder Land podcast last year, wrote, “I swear I believed Mrs Dolly was immortal. Some people are so extraordinary, their existence feels almost impossible. Dolly was one of those people. A once-in-a-lifetime soul. A woman whose light, heart, talent and humanity changed this world forever. To have admired her was a gift. To have met her, spent time in her presence, and somehow been lucky enough that Dolly Parton knew my name… I will never have words big enough for what that means to me.”

 @khloekardashian / Via Instagram: @https://www.instagram.com/reels/DL46liaRaln/

“What an astronomical human being. What a legacy. What a loss. There will never be another Dolly,” she added alongside a string of broken heart emojis.

 Jennifer Lopez wrote under Dolly’s Instagram page, “A masterclass in lighting up the whole world by being your true authentic self. With song, humor and love she made our lives and our world a better more beautiful place. I will miss you Dolly 🤍”

 BEHROUZ MEHRI / Getty Images

 Kelly Clarkson said, “Dolly Parton had a way of making everyone feel special, and seen, and welcomed, and as if you were old friends. I will miss her heart and her voice as I am sure millions will. What an incredible gift and talent she was and still is with an amazing catalogue of art she has left behind for all of us.”

 Variety / Getty Images

 Octavia Spencer wrote, “Dolly you were a gift to the world, your voice, your philanthropic heart, and warmth made us a feel seen and that the world was a pretty decent place. We miss you.”

 Variety / Getty Images

 Kristin Chenoweth wrote, “Like the rest of the world, I’m immediately heartbroken. I met Dolly on several occasions and she always made me feel like one of her own. She even agreed to sing with me on one of my records. My ultimate inspiration. The world has lost one of the best but I know we will never forget her because she is impossible to forget. I love you Dolly and I will ALWAYS love you. 💔🌈🦋”

 Jeff Vespa / Getty Images

 Ex-Dancing with the Stars champion Derek Hough said, “Heartbroken to hear about the passing of Dolly Parton. She was an absolute icon, a true legend not just for her music, but for her spirit, her kindness, her joy, her light. I was lucky enough to share the stage with her, something I will never take for granted. Her music and the way she made people feel will live on forever. Sending love to all she touched. Thank you, Dolly. You will never be forgotten ♥️”

 Richard Cartwright / Getty Images

 Megan Hilty wrote, “She made more of an impact on me than I can express in an Instagram post and this deep and profound loss will take quite some time to process. I am so grateful to have been in her orbit and we are all so lucky this actual angel walked among us. 🦋”

 Joe Kohen / Getty Images

 Carol Burnett, who starred with Dolly in the 1979 TV special Dolly & Carol in Nashville, described shooting the special as one of her “favorite memories.” “I’m so sad right now…We shot the week of Thanksgiving and Dolly made individual turkey dinners for every one of us, that she cooked herself. We were a family. That’s who she was,” she wrote on Instagram.

 CBS Photo Archive / Getty Images

 Posting a sweet photo with the late icon, Ethan Hawke said, “I got to meet Dolly Parton, and everything everyone is saying about her was true. Deep, serious, playful, loving, wise…. A woman of integrity. A North Star. She knew how to make a positive impact and have a laugh while doing it. I left her presence lighter and charged to be better.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @ethanhawke / Via instagram.com

 Sarah Jessica Parker wrote, “No!!!!!! I never met @dollyparton but my gosh, did I love her. I don’t think any of us had to know her to love her. One of the greatest this country ever produced.”

 Michael Buckner / Getty Images

“Legend. For real. Forever. And always advocating for those she knew and understood needed a champion,” she continued. “What a loss. But aren’t we so lucky,so fortunate for the endless gifts she shared. With the world. Godspeed and RIP. You will be terribly missed.”

 Drew Barrymore shared a past interaction from her self-titled talk show with Dolly, during which the country music star preached about love and acceptance. “@dollyparton will always be loved & remembered 🩷” Drew captioned the post.

 View this photo on Instagram

 The Drew Barrymore Show / Via instagram.com

 Jason Earles, who starred with Dolly, Billy Ray, and Miley in Disney Channel’s Hannah Montana, wrote, “I’m thinking about every wonderful thing I’ve ever heard about Dolly. All her success, every personal story, all the posts people have made today in tribute…and all together, it barely scratches the surface of what a wonderful person she was. I’m so grateful I got to call her Aunt Dolly on the show. But the truth is, no matter who you were, she always made you feel like family. I was a fan my whole life and I’ll always cherish the little time I got to spend with her. My love to everyone else out there who’s feeling the loss of our Aunt Dolly.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @realdukeofearles / Via instagram.com

 Singer Kesha paid tribute to Dolly on stage during her Pittsburgh concert on Aug. 25, performing a cover of the late star’s 1980 song “Old Flames (Can’t Hold a Candle to You). “I just want to say thank you for bringing me so much joy today, because earlier today, I’m sure many of y’all know that we lost Ms. Dolly Parton,” Kesha told the crowd. “We literally lost an angel. But through her art and through her kindness and through her love, she will live forever. And I want to talk about her a little bit. For those of you who don’t know, I come from a long lineage of songwriters and before I was born, my mom actually wrote a song for Dolly Parton. And that song bought us a house, like a roof. That song put me through school.”

 James Smith/Sam Snap / Getty Images

 Katy Perry said on Instagram, "Like the rest of the world, my heart sank seeing the news of dear Dolly’s passing. She meant so much to so many people for so long. For me, she was an example of a woman who defied the stereotypes for decades. She proved that big boobs, big brains, and a big voice can all exist in one tiny body! But the biggest thing about her by far was her heart."

 Christopher Polk/ACM2016 / Getty Images

"I had the honor of meeting and singing with her several times. Every time I saw Dolly, she was a pure, sweet (but not saccharine) sassy, cup of joy," she continued. "Her way of looking at life with a sense of humor has always been an inspiration to me… I remember having a dream of having her sing with me for my Super Bowl show, popping out of a larger than life rhinestone cowboy boot… and though she couldn’t do it at the time she sent my team a sweet note, through fax… it was 2015! lol."Katy added, "If there’s someone you wanna look up to and model your life after, it’s Dolly. Dolly was glam, funny, and kind as fuck. Her star will forever shine bright and I bet you she’s already remodeling them pearly gates with rhinestones. We will always love you Dolly!"

 Tim McGraw wrote on Instagram, “She was an icon and showed us all what was possible, not only as a human but as an entertainer. She was the blueprint, head and shoulders above anyone that came before her and all those of us that have come after. Everything she did, she did it with kindness, grace and that famous wit and smile. It’s been hard to not be in tears all day. There will never be another Dolly Parton.”

 Jason Kempin / Getty Images

 Sharing a photo of himself and Dolly on The Voice, Blake Shelton wrote, “I can say with absolute certainty that we are all feeling the same heart brokenness today. I only got to spend any real time with Dolly when Gwen [Stefani] and I got to work with her on The Voice. I want everyone to know that she was the EXACT person that you think she is. It was like being with the funnest, most loving, most caring and closest member of your family. Truly a loss for the entire world. We love you Dolly.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @blakeshelton / Trae Patton / NBCU Photo Bank / NBCUniversal via Getty Images via Getty Images

 Zac Brown shared on Instagram, “She was a real angel long before now. Her faith was number one. There will never be another Dolly Parton. Pure talent, pure soul, pure love. She lived by example. My wife and I are heartbroken but so blessed to know her heart. Dolly is a national treasure. She sang her heart out on Butterfly, and I will never forget the first time that I heard what she sang on it and how much she loved that song.”

 Jeff Kravitz / Getty Images

“Our hearts go out to her family, her team, and all of her friends. I believe she would want us to celebrate her life, be true to who we are, and show each other love and kindness. She loved Jesus and lived like He did, by example. Thank you, Dolly, for all the love and music you put into this world. You will live on in your songs and in all of our hearts,” the post added.

 Singer-songwriter Brandi Carlile shared a lengthy, heartwarming statement honoring the late star, which began, “Dolly traded in her butterfly wings today. I felt her leaving all week and I’ve been singing ‘Coat Of Many Colors’ with I’m With Her and asking folks to pray everyday. I don’t even know why. She took my face in her hands and prayed over me once. I’ve never been the same since. Her prayers were maybe more powerful than mine or anyone else’s, because that prayer has had a very long rainbow colored halo and I hope it lasts me my whole life.”

 Kevin Mazur / Getty Images

“Dolly had a way of deeply belonging to every one of us, and yet somehow still not being of this world. There’s really only one other person in human history I can think of who has held that light,” she wrote in part.“Before I met her, I loved her because she took a risk and accepted me (and all of us) for being gay in a time where she didn’t need to say anything. And she has been asked to comment and speak on MANY things over the years… choosing only to speak on that which brings love and mercy to real people, and shutting down any line of questioning that won’t. She never wavered on accepting anyone for who they were and who they were meant to be,” she said. “After I met her, I loved her for being obscenely generous, whip smart and possessing the kind of otherworldly discernment I’ll never stop chasing.”Brandi added, “And yet I’m nobody and everyone all at once. Just a heartbroken Dolly fan at the end of the day with a head full of memories, prayers and songs left behind by a big breasted angel with a twinkle in her eye and the whole world in her hands.”

 Colman Domingo said, “Dolly taught us that you can be anything and do anything and to do it with kindness. What a light. We are all grateful that we lived in a time of Dolly Parton. We will always love her.”

 Araya Doheny / Getty Images

 Kevin Costner, who personally sought Dolly’s permission to use her 1973 song “I Will Always Love You” in the 1992 film The Bodyguard, wrote on Instagram, “Oh my goodness! Where did you go Dolly? We are all breathless. The feeling of who you are and who you were are so close,” he wrote. “We have all stopped for a moment to think of the miracle that was you. Thank you for trusting me with ‘I Will Always Love You.’ So gracious in all things. We are all at a loss this moment. Forgive us but we will miss you so much. So much.”

 ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection

 Retired musician Linda Ronstadt made a rare public statement to honor Dolly’s passing. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my friend, Dolly Parton. One of the most extraordinary musical experiences of my life was recording with her. The world is a poorer place without her,” she wrote on Facebook.

 New York Daily News Archive / Getty Images

 Amazon founder and multibillionaire Jeff Bezos wrote, “Dolly spent her whole life showing us what it means to lead with love. Lauren [Sánchez Bezos] and I are so grateful to have known her. She lifted everyone with her music, her generosity, and her joy. Sending our sincere condolences to her family and everyone she touched.”

 Anadolu / Getty Images

 The CEO of Apple, Tim Cook, wrote on X, “Dolly Parton’s music helped light up the world. She was a brilliant songwriter, cultural icon, and dedicated philanthropist who helped instill a love of reading and learning in millions of children around the world. May she rest in peace.”

 @tim_cook / Via x.com

 Harvey Mason Jr., CEO of The Recording Academy, shared, “It’s nearly impossible to fully capture the depth of what Dolly Parton means to the world...Through her unwavering dedication to philanthropy, she gave back to her community and to the world with the same heart that defined her music. On behalf of the Recording Academy, our thoughts are with Dolly’s family, friends and the countless fans whose lives she touched. Her legacy – one of talent, kindness and resilience – will endure for generations to come.”

 Rebecca Sapp / Getty Images

 Bill Anderson, who bagged a Grammy nomination with Dolly in 2022 for their song “Someday It’ll All Make Sense (Bluegrass Version),” reflected on his last conversation with Dolly in a heartfelt Instagram post. “The last thing Dolly said to me was, ‘Bill Anderson – I will Always Love You,’” he recalled. “She was looking me in the eye from the giant video screen in the the Grand Ole Opry House on the occasion of my 65th Opry Anniversary a few weeks ago. She was smiling as only Dolly could, making my night even more special than it already was. The news of her passing has rocked my world, but as we sang together back in 2023, ‘Someday It’ll All Make Sense.’”

 Tony R. Phipps / Getty Images

 SAG-AFTRA president Sean Astin said in part, “The passing of Dolly Parton will be deeply felt throughout our membership. Her life and legacy of joy and creativity had an indescribable impact on the world. As a singer, songwriter, performer, business leader and all-around visionary, Dolly Parton’s talent is revered across generations. Her basic humanity is known to the world and she is simply beloved by countless millions. Personally, from 9 to 5 when she effortlessly advanced the cause of professional women, to her Islands in the Stream collaboration with Kenny Rogers, I’m a true and forever fan. On behalf of SAG-AFTRA and my family, we send thoughts of love and condolences to her family.”

 Terry Wyatt / Getty Images

 Keke Palmer wrote, “I’m devastated. Truly.”

 @keke / Via instagram.com

 John Stamos said, “Shine on, Dolly. We will miss you.”

 NBC / Getty Images

 Rosie O’Donnell wrote, “This earth angel has gone back to heaven where she came from - heartbroken 💔 #iwillalwaysloveyou”

 Randy Holmes / Getty Images

 Kyle Richards said, “Thank you for all the joy you brought to so many 🙏 Rest in Peace 🤍 💔”

 Cindy Ord / Getty Images

 Paris Hilton was one of several celebs who paid tribute to Dolly directly under the late star’s Instagram page. “Forever my icon 👸🏼💫 You will be missed🥹,” she wrote.

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Olivia Munn wrote, "I will always love you ❤️❤️❤️❤️"

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Luke Evans commented, “Rest in plush cotton dear Dolly we will always love you ❤️” — a reference to Dolly’s nephew’s revelation that her final wish was to be laid to rest in a “beautiful bed of plush cotton.”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Sophia Bush wrote, “This one cuts deep. What an icon. What a humanitarian. What A GAL. We love you, Dolly.”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Kelsea Ballerini commented, “one of one. thank you dolly. 🦋”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Donatella Versace wrote, “We’ll never forget you, Dolly 🤍,” and, "An icon. She will be missed 🤍🕊️"

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Our thoughts are with Dolly’s family and loved ones.

This post is being updated.
news.author: Leyla Mohammed

news.title: Celebrities React To Dolly Parton's Death
news.text:
On Aug. 25, news broke that beloved country music icon and philanthropist Dolly Parton had sadly died at age 80.

 NBC / Getty Images

 Dolly’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, made the announcement in a video shared to Instagram on behalf of the Parton family. “This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality,” he said. “As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment, but haven't truly felt it until now.”

 Silver Screen Collection / Getty Images

“Dolly opened doors not just for me, but for her entire family to reach the potential we didn't even know was possible,” Bryan added in part. “Dolly also opened doors for generations of singers, songwriters, musicians, and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent. By her example, we believed that anything was possible. She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the doors she opened made and changed history.”

 The news of Dolly’s death comes just days after the star issued an update on her health issues, which she began to publicly address after the death of her husband, Carl Dean, in March 2025.

 View this photo on Instagram

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

“As I’ve shared in video messages throughout the past year, I am dealing with some health issues that I just didn’t pay attention to when I was watching over Carl,” she told People on Aug. 21. “Even though I’m still healin’, I’m still workin’! You know me — as I’ve often said — I’ve dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I’m gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life.”

 In the wake of the heartbreaking news, here’s how celebrities across the globe are mourning Dolly’s passing:

 Billy Ray Cyrus — whose decadeslong friendship with Dolly made her godmother to his daughter, Miley Cyrus — wrote on Instagram: “I have so many moments and memories with Dolly, it’s hard to know where to start. Like every little boy, I grew up loving Dolly Parton. She was a part of our lives, on our TV’s, right in our living rooms. In 1992, I’ll never forget walking into her dressing room to apologize for all the tabloid stories which claimed I was having an affair with her. In true Dolly fashion, she just looked at me, winked and said, ‘Honey, this trash sells records!’”

 Michael Kovac / Getty Images

“Dolly recently sent me a beautiful message, telling me she loved me with her whole heart,” he said. “I will always love her in the same way ….. with my whole heart … and I always will.”

 2. Country star Kacey Musgraves shared a series of tweets about the heartbreaking news, beginning: “Dolly. 💔 This really really hurts.” She then followed up, “The world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden,” and, “So glad she’s with her Carl Dean. No one talk to me today.”Dolly. 💔 This really really hurts.— K A C E Y (@KaceyMusgraves) August 25, 2026

K A C E Y / Via x.com

 The world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden.— K A C E Y (@KaceyMusgraves) August 25, 2026

K A C E Y / Via x.com

 So glad she’s with her Carl Dean. No one talk to me today.— K A C E Y (@KaceyMusgraves) August 25, 2026

K A C E Y / Via x.com

 Beyoncé, who collaborated with Dolly on her 2024 country album Cowboy Carter, wrote via her website: “Dolly, you were the barometer. The north star. Bold and brilliant. Talented and tenacious. You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself. I am grateful for your art, your heart, your generosity, your humor, your entrepreneurship. I’m honored that I had the privilege to work with you. I will treasure that forever. Thank you for your profound impact on the world. You are an angel who has made this world a happier place because of your joyful art. You are truly one of one. Rest peacefully.”

 Michael Buckner / Getty Images

 Taylor Swift said in a statement shared with People, “A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right. But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted.”

 TheStewartofNY / Getty Images

“Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist,” she continued.“Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too,” Taylor concluded, adding, “Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.”

 Shania Twain wrote on Instagram, “Dolly was pure light sent from heaven. My mentor is gone. My songwriting teacher and hero of grace and humility. There is a hole in my heart but the joy of just the thought of her smile will continue to fill me with inspiration for as long as I live. I will cherish this moment performing Coat Of Many Colors with Dolly forever. Goodbye Dolly. Rest in peace, beautiful angel.”

 Scott Suchman / Getty Images

 Carrie Underwood said, “She’s not gone. I know exactly where she is. She was the epitome of faith, grace, talent, beauty and humor. She had a humble heart for Jesus and made everyone around her feel special. She was probably the one person on planet Earth that everyone loved and could agree on. She was a one of one and no one will ever come close. It’s alright to be sad that this world lost a legend, but heaven gained an angel. Well done, good and faithful Dolly. Welcome home. ❤️🦋”

 Rick Diamond / Getty Images

 Reese Witherspoon wrote on Instagram, “I count my lucky stars that I called Dolly my friend. When I was playing June Carter Cash in Walk the Line, she took me to dinner and told me stories of how June Carter charmed everyone in country music. Dolly gave me the courage to put my whole spirit into that performance and made me see how lucky I was to be a storyteller. Throughout my entire career, she sent me little notes of encouragement and support, telling me to be the light in people’s lives and listen to my angels. Always signed: ‘I will always love you.’ 🦋”

 Michael Kovac / Getty Images

“Dolly, I miss you already. Your talent, your wisdom and your beautiful spirit lit up our lives. Go soar with your angels…. We will always love you. ❤️,” she added.

 Sally Field, who starred with Dolly in the 1989 film Steel Magnolias, wrote, “If there are truly angels on earth, then we have just lost one. Dolly Parton. There will never be another. I adored her with all my heart and will always cherish our time together. Forever. Rest in peace beautiful Dolly.”

 Amanda Edwards / Getty Images

 Fellow Steel Magnolias actor Julia Roberts purportedly said in a statement, “Dolly was a magical and joyous human. I hold knowing her as a treasure in my life. The sun has dimmed today.”

 Ron Galella, Ltd. / Getty Images

 Barbra Streisand wrote, “So sorry to hear about Dolly - she was a true force of nature. May she rest in peace 😢.”

 PATRICK T. FALLON / Getty Images

 Goldie Hawn shared a throwback photo of herself and Dolly and said, “This was the first day I met Dolly. She was a ray of light! Even then, she was lit up like an angel, a joyful, celestial being. Dolly blessed us all for generations to come. Rest, dear Angel, and, as you said, keep the angels creating music and singing in the heavens. 🕊️❤️”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @goldiehawn / Via instagram.com

 Brooke Shields wrote, “Dolly, there will never be anyone else like you. I am gutted to hear the news. The world will forever be indebted to the good you’ve done and the legacy you’ve left. The equilibrium of the earth feels off. Thank you for everything.”

 Dia Dipasupil / Getty Images

 Bette Midler said, “Our beloved Dolly Parton has died. I am devastated, and I’m sure the nation will mourn her as I do, and for many years to come. She had a voice of pure gold and a heart to match. What a terrible, terrible loss.”

 Bruce Glikas / Getty Images

 Sarah Michelle Gellar shared an old clip from Watch What Happens Live, in which Dolly talked about being an uncredited producer on Buffy the Vampire Slayer. “Just being a small part of the great history of @dollyparton is everything to me,” Sarah wrote.

 Richard Cartwright / TM and Copyright ©20th Century Fox Film Corp. All rights reserved / courtesy Everett Collection

 WWHL host Andy Cohen shared a photo of a rhinestone Dolly Parton canvas and wrote, “This painting hangs in my living room. One day Ben [his son] said ‘Daddy, is that God?’ He was onto something…🦋 💔 We were all so lucky to live in her midst and get to experience her music, kindness, and joy. 💔 🦋”

 Rick Diamond / Getty Images

 Jimmy Fallon wrote, “I was lucky enough to know and work with the one and only Dolly Parton. She was a phenomenal guest on the show; always funny and always made everyone she met feel like a million dollars. We did duets together, laughed together and danced through Dollywood in the Smoky Mountains of Pigeon Forge. And even though we did all that, I would still get butterflies just being in her presence. And that’s kind of what I think of when I think of Dolly. She’s a butterfly. Beautiful. Magical. Dreamy. And like most butterflies, they stay for a moment - captivate you, fascinate you, mesmerize you and then fly away far too soon. I love you Dolly. I will always miss you.”

 NBC / Getty Images

 17. Sabrina Carpenter — whose heartwarming interaction with Dolly about aging went viral last year, not long after they collaborated — wrote, “oh dolly 💔 the only thing i could say after we first met was ‘she really is an angel walking the earth’ and ‘we look like we could be sisters!’ i will cherish our laughter and conversations and i will keep your wisdom, your playful outlook on life, and perfect sense of humor in my pocket for the rainy days. there will never be another you and how lucky are we all to have experienced your singular magic as well as your once in a lifetime voice, songs, and heart.” @sabrinacarpenter this is too good sorry @Dolly Parton ♬ original sound - Betches @sabrinacarpenter / Via tiktok.com

“your light will be something the world will search forever to find again 🦋🦋🦋 i will always love you,” she added.

 Musician Diane Warren said, “A light has gone out in the world. A light we need now more than ever. How can this even be???? Not Dolly!!! Not beautiful brilliant Dolly!!!!! I found this picture of Dolly and my Mom Flora when I was inducted into the Songwriters Hall Of Fame in 2021 She was excited for me but I think a lot more excited to meet Dolly! Im so honored that I got to work with her, abd will aways cherish that. What a sad sad day not just for tve world of music, but for the world. We will always love You.🎶🎵💔”

 L. Cohen / Getty Images

 Connie Britton wrote, “I keep having these conversations with Dolly in my head today, like I did back in those Nashville days at the Ryman until I actually finally got to meet her in 2022. So today I’ve been telling her what an inspiration and godsend she has been to me and to so many. And she says, ‘You know honey, God is in you. Know and love every part of yourself. Let it shine as only you can. Use everything you’ve been given, all that you’ve come from. And use it generously, for joy and honesty and fun and service.’ At least, yeah…that’s what she’s saying to me. Thank you Dolly.”

 Arturo Holmes / Getty Images

Connie then referenced her Nashville costar Hayden Panettiere’s recent death as she added, “The blonds are really taking heaven by storm this week. 💔”

 Heidi Klum wrote, “Dolly I will miss you. We will all miss you. You were an idol to me and so many other people around the world - your generosity and talent are unparalleled. It was an honor to share a couch with you and to learn how to use my nails to make music. I will always love you. ❤️”

 NBC / Getty Images

 Jane Fonda, who starred with Dolly in the 1980 comedy 9 to 5, wrote, “I am devastated. I just learned that Dolly has moved on. I know that millions are mourning and I want to say this – more than anyone I have ever known, Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful that she is woven into all our lives and hearts forever.”

 New York Daily News Archive / Getty Images

“I never knew anyone like her. She was simultaneously a naughty, playful southern gal from the hollows of Tennessee and a deep, soulful thinker who could see through people right down to their true selves,” she later continued. “She was many things…lyricist, songstress, player of many instruments, writer, prankster, visionary, loyal friend, who’d never go to bed before she and her friends had laughed so hard they’d have to cross their legs.”“To her gay and trans fans, I want you to know that she loved you. You know that without me telling you. She loved all her fans and they are legion. And you know she doesn’t want y’all to mourn now. Dress up and celebrate her spirit. But first, watch the final episode of Grace and Frankie where she’s an Angel, the head honcho working class angel in Heaven,” she added. “RIP, beautiful woman. We love you. ❤️”

 Fellow 9 to 5 star Lily Tomlin shared an old photo of herself and Dolly, captioned, “No words…💔”

 Kevin Winter / Getty Images

 Sharing a photo of a sweet, congratulatory note he received from Dolly when he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, rapper Eminem wrote on Instagram, “I’m sorry we never got a chance to meet, but getting this note from Dolly really had a an impact on me. She definitely didn’t have to take the time to do it. Even for a kid who mostly listened to rap music, she was an icon. A superstar in every sense. Rest easy Dolly. And thank you for the kind words.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @eminem / Via instagram.com

 24. Former President Barack Obama said in a social media statement, “It’s hard to imagine many people having a bigger impact than Dolly Parton. Born in a one-room cabin, she earned 11 Grammys and an Emmy, built a business empire, helped millions of kids learn to read, and — as if that wasn’t enough — helped accelerate the research that led to the Moderna COVID vaccine. What a life. Michelle and I are thinking of Dolly’s family and her many, many fans.”It’s hard to imagine many people having a bigger impact than Dolly Parton. Born in a one-room cabin, she earned 11 Grammys and an Emmy, built a business empire, helped millions of kids learn to read, and — as if that wasn’t enough — helped accelerate the research that led to the… https://t.co/gl4KGm4vnk— Barack Obama (@BarackObama) August 25, 2026

Barack Obama / Via x.com

 George W. Bush also reflected on Dolly’s legacy in a statement shared on X. “Laura [Bush] and I, along with thousands of her fans, mourn the passing of Dolly Parton. We loved her music and her style. She was a great entertainer and even greater person. We respected her work to promote literacy, advance health, and strengthen communities. Dolly was a talented and hardworking American who will be missed,” he said.

 Bloomberg / Getty Images

 26. Former President Bill Clinton wrote, “Dolly Parton was one of a kind—a great songwriter and performer who told the stories of everyday Americans with honesty, humility, and heart. She rose high from her East Tennessee roots and never forgot where she came from. And she always believed in giving back, especially in her efforts to promote literacy. Hillary and I were big fans and first saw her in 1974, and will always be grateful for the music and the memories. Our thoughts and prayers are with her family, her legion of fans, and everyone who loved her.”Dolly Parton was one of a kind—a great songwriter and performer who told the stories of everyday Americans with honesty, humility, and heart. She rose high from her East Tennessee roots and never forgot where she came from. And she always believed in giving back, especially in…— Bill Clinton (@BillClinton) August 25, 2026

Bill Clinton / Via x.com

 27. Former Secretary of State, Hillary, added, “Dolly Parton did all the good she could, for all the people she could, for as long as ever she could. From her legendary songwriting to the Imagination Library—which sent 1 million books a month to children across the country—she was the best of America. Dolly, we'll miss your great heart.”— Hillary Clinton (@HillaryClinton) August 25, 2026

Hillary Clinton / Via x.com

 Current US President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to honor Dolly. “Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away. This is a true loss for millions of people,” he said. “There has never been anyone like her, and never will. In her honor, I am lowering the American flag throughout the United States for a one week period beginning tonight at 6:00PM. Rest in Peace, Dolly! The World loves you.”

 Finn Gomez / Getty Images

 Former Vice President Kamala Harris said, “Dolly Parton was a true American icon. First introduced to the world as a ‘little girl from up in East Tennessee,’ she became a global superstar. Her career accolades included 11 Grammy awards, an Emmy, an honorary Oscar, and — my favorite — more than 300 million books sent to millions of children around the world through her Imagination Library. All at once she was kind, modest, and funny. With her music, her philanthropy, and her style, Dolly was one of one.”

 Frazer Harrison / Getty Images

“Doug [Emhoff] and I send our prayers to her family, friends, and all those who have been touched by her magic. We will always love you, Dolly,” she added.

 NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani said on X, “This is truly heartbreaking. Dolly Parton was an extraordinary person and an irreplaceable champion of the working class. We are a better country because of her.”

 Michael M. Santiago / Getty Images

 Oprah Winfrey shared a throwback photo with Dolly and said, “One of my fondest memories with @dollyparton: Having a hoot and a holler while wearing Bob Mackie gowns on her show Dolly. This girl from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee dreamed a life and then lived a life bigger than she could have ever imagined, giving so generously to others in ways we saw and ways we didn’t. No one like her. She brought the light, and we are all better because she was here. God bless you, Dolly—you earned your wings🪽”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @oprah / Jerry Fitzgerald/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images

 Jamie Lee Curtis posted a photo with Dolly and wrote, “They say don't meet your heroes. They were wrong about her. Her bravery to know that she was more than they thought she was and that she needed to break away and move on into new work and new possibilities led her to write I WILL ALWAYS LOVE YOU, as her way of thanking and loving, but moving on. She is a great example for us all.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @jamieleecurtis / Via instagram.com

 Céline Dion wrote, “Dolly…you were pure light, with a kind heart and a generous spirit. We will now be missing one of the most joyful voices this world has ever known. Thank you for the music, the laughter, and the love you gave us all. We will always love you.”

 Bruce Bennett / Getty Images

 Paul McCartney said, “The magnificent star Dolly Parton has died and it is so sad. She was such a wonderful woman. I first met her in Nashville at the Grand Ole Opry where she had been playing with the country star Porter Wagoner and was about to start her solo career. She was so bubbly and full of life it is difficult to take in the news that she has passed. Her songwriting, her singing and her philanthropy were unrivaled in the world of country music and it is hard to imagine living in a world without Dolly.”

 Jim Dyson / Getty Images

“She was a very clever business woman who understood the value of her music and, most importantly, the effect that she had on the people of the world,” he continued. “There was no greater honour for me than to have her sing my song Let It Be and, even though I only made a small contribution to it, I am so honoured that she did it. I am so proud to have known her and admire her unique talents. Thanks Dolly for the beautiful music you gave me and the whole world. We will always love you, god bless and rest in peace. You were the best.”

 Posting a photo of himself and Dolly on stage, Elton John wrote, “Shocked and devastated to hear of Dolly’s passing. A giant of an artist - unique and irreplaceable, with the kindest heart.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @eltonjohn / Michael Loccisano / FilmMagic for Country Music Association

 Keith Urban shared an Instagram Story that read, “heartbroken today…Dolly Parton💔 honestly…I have no words right now.”

 @keithurban / Via Instagram: @https://www.instagram.com/keithurban/?hl=en

 In a statement shared with NBC News, per TODAY, singer Patti LaBelle said, “I am deeply saddened by the loss of my dear friend who was loved by all. Dolly’s artistry, brilliance, and extraordinary life inspired so many people, including me. Her light will forever shine! I send my deepest condolences to all of her loved ones and fans all over the world!”

 Erika Goldring / Getty Images

 Country star Reba McEntire wrote on Instagram, “Well, I just got the news that my buddy Dolly passed onto the higher and greater side. Dolly, thank you for all the wonderful things you did for us here on earth. Your love, your music and you gave so much with your huge huge heart. There will never ever be another you.”

 Kevin Winter / Getty Images

“We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang. Thank you, Lord, for Dolly. She’s gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her,” Reba said. “I’ll never forget the first time I met you and I’ll never forget our last conversation. I hold it with love in my heart.”

 Darlene Love said, “I’m truly heartbroken. This one really hurts. 💔 Dolly Parton was one of a kind — an extraordinary talent, a beautiful soul, and a woman whose music, kindness and spirit touched generations. Her light will continue to shine through the incredible legacy she leaves behind. Rest in peace, Dolly. You will be deeply missed and forever loved. ❤️🙏🏽”

 Jason Mendez / Getty Images

 Dionne Warwick wrote, “I will certainly miss her laugher, jokes and her being. Rest well and in total peace my friend. My heart is heavy.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @dionnewarwick / Kind Music Group / Via youtube.com

 Seth MacFarlane wrote, “The news of Dolly Parton’s passing is devastating. I had the extraordinary experience of working with her on The Orville, and it was a joy to discover that she really was exactly the person we all hoped she was. Her kindness, generosity, and authenticity were evident from moment one, and the benign yet assured command she maintained over her empire was obvious from the genuine love and trust you could see from everyone who worked for her. The world is a dimmer place today without her.”

 Rich Polk / Getty Images

 Mick Jagger said, “What a wonderful songwriter and singer Dolly was. She brought so many people together, we will all miss her so much.”

 Allan Tannenbaum / Getty Images

 The Jacksons shared a statement that read, “We are deeply saddened by the passing of the incomparable Dolly Parton. Dolly was a true trailblazer. Through her extraordinary talent, kindness and generosity, she opened doors and inspired generations around the world…Thank you, Dolly, for the music, the joy and the light you shared with us all. May you rest peacefully in the loving arms of the Lord, reunited with your husband Carl and the many loved ones who made their journey to Heaven before you.”

 Sebastian Reuter / Getty Images

“Our prayers are with Dolly’s family, friends and everyone whose life she touched. Rest in peace, Dolly. Your beautiful spirit and remarkable legacy will live on forever. 🙏🏾🕊️,” they added.

 Khloé Kardashian, who featured Dolly as a guest on her Khloé in Wonder Land podcast last year, wrote, “I swear I believed Mrs Dolly was immortal. Some people are so extraordinary, their existence feels almost impossible. Dolly was one of those people. A once-in-a-lifetime soul. A woman whose light, heart, talent and humanity changed this world forever. To have admired her was a gift. To have met her, spent time in her presence, and somehow been lucky enough that Dolly Parton knew my name… I will never have words big enough for what that means to me.”

 @khloekardashian / Via Instagram: @https://www.instagram.com/reels/DL46liaRaln/

“What an astronomical human being. What a legacy. What a loss. There will never be another Dolly,” she added alongside a string of broken heart emojis.

 Jennifer Lopez wrote under Dolly’s Instagram page, “A masterclass in lighting up the whole world by being your true authentic self. With song, humor and love she made our lives and our world a better more beautiful place. I will miss you Dolly 🤍”

 BEHROUZ MEHRI / Getty Images

 Kelly Clarkson said, “Dolly Parton had a way of making everyone feel special, and seen, and welcomed, and as if you were old friends. I will miss her heart and her voice as I am sure millions will. What an incredible gift and talent she was and still is with an amazing catalogue of art she has left behind for all of us.”

 Variety / Getty Images

 Octavia Spencer wrote, “Dolly you were a gift to the world, your voice, your philanthropic heart, and warmth made us a feel seen and that the world was a pretty decent place. We miss you.”

 Variety / Getty Images

 Kristin Chenoweth wrote, “Like the rest of the world, I’m immediately heartbroken. I met Dolly on several occasions and she always made me feel like one of her own. She even agreed to sing with me on one of my records. My ultimate inspiration. The world has lost one of the best but I know we will never forget her because she is impossible to forget. I love you Dolly and I will ALWAYS love you. 💔🌈🦋”

 Jeff Vespa / Getty Images

 Ex-Dancing with the Stars champion Derek Hough said, “Heartbroken to hear about the passing of Dolly Parton. She was an absolute icon, a true legend not just for her music, but for her spirit, her kindness, her joy, her light. I was lucky enough to share the stage with her, something I will never take for granted. Her music and the way she made people feel will live on forever. Sending love to all she touched. Thank you, Dolly. You will never be forgotten ♥️”

 Richard Cartwright / Getty Images

 Megan Hilty wrote, “She made more of an impact on me than I can express in an Instagram post and this deep and profound loss will take quite some time to process. I am so grateful to have been in her orbit and we are all so lucky this actual angel walked among us. 🦋”

 Joe Kohen / Getty Images

 Carol Burnett, who starred with Dolly in the 1979 TV special Dolly & Carol in Nashville, described shooting the special as one of her “favorite memories.” “I’m so sad right now…We shot the week of Thanksgiving and Dolly made individual turkey dinners for every one of us, that she cooked herself. We were a family. That’s who she was,” she wrote on Instagram.

 CBS Photo Archive / Getty Images

 Posting a sweet photo with the late icon, Ethan Hawke said, “I got to meet Dolly Parton, and everything everyone is saying about her was true. Deep, serious, playful, loving, wise…. A woman of integrity. A North Star. She knew how to make a positive impact and have a laugh while doing it. I left her presence lighter and charged to be better.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @ethanhawke / Via instagram.com

 Sarah Jessica Parker wrote, “No!!!!!! I never met @dollyparton but my gosh, did I love her. I don’t think any of us had to know her to love her. One of the greatest this country ever produced.”

 Michael Buckner / Getty Images

“Legend. For real. Forever. And always advocating for those she knew and understood needed a champion,” she continued. “What a loss. But aren’t we so lucky,so fortunate for the endless gifts she shared. With the world. Godspeed and RIP. You will be terribly missed.”

 Drew Barrymore shared a past interaction from her self-titled talk show with Dolly, during which the country music star preached about love and acceptance. “@dollyparton will always be loved & remembered 🩷” Drew captioned the post.

 View this photo on Instagram

 The Drew Barrymore Show / Via instagram.com

 Jason Earles, who starred with Dolly, Billy Ray, and Miley in Disney Channel’s Hannah Montana, wrote, “I’m thinking about every wonderful thing I’ve ever heard about Dolly. All her success, every personal story, all the posts people have made today in tribute…and all together, it barely scratches the surface of what a wonderful person she was. I’m so grateful I got to call her Aunt Dolly on the show. But the truth is, no matter who you were, she always made you feel like family. I was a fan my whole life and I’ll always cherish the little time I got to spend with her. My love to everyone else out there who’s feeling the loss of our Aunt Dolly.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @realdukeofearles / Via instagram.com

 Singer Kesha paid tribute to Dolly on stage during her Pittsburgh concert on Aug. 25, performing a cover of the late star’s 1980 song “Old Flames (Can’t Hold a Candle to You). “I just want to say thank you for bringing me so much joy today, because earlier today, I’m sure many of y’all know that we lost Ms. Dolly Parton,” Kesha told the crowd. “We literally lost an angel. But through her art and through her kindness and through her love, she will live forever. And I want to talk about her a little bit. For those of you who don’t know, I come from a long lineage of songwriters and before I was born, my mom actually wrote a song for Dolly Parton. And that song bought us a house, like a roof. That song put me through school.”

 James Smith/Sam Snap / Getty Images

 Katy Perry said on Instagram, "Like the rest of the world, my heart sank seeing the news of dear Dolly’s passing. She meant so much to so many people for so long. For me, she was an example of a woman who defied the stereotypes for decades. She proved that big boobs, big brains, and a big voice can all exist in one tiny body! But the biggest thing about her by far was her heart."

 Christopher Polk/ACM2016 / Getty Images

"I had the honor of meeting and singing with her several times. Every time I saw Dolly, she was a pure, sweet (but not saccharine) sassy, cup of joy," she continued. "Her way of looking at life with a sense of humor has always been an inspiration to me… I remember having a dream of having her sing with me for my Super Bowl show, popping out of a larger than life rhinestone cowboy boot… and though she couldn’t do it at the time she sent my team a sweet note, through fax… it was 2015! lol."Katy added, "If there’s someone you wanna look up to and model your life after, it’s Dolly. Dolly was glam, funny, and kind as fuck. Her star will forever shine bright and I bet you she’s already remodeling them pearly gates with rhinestones. We will always love you Dolly!"

 Tim McGraw wrote on Instagram, “She was an icon and showed us all what was possible, not only as a human but as an entertainer. She was the blueprint, head and shoulders above anyone that came before her and all those of us that have come after. Everything she did, she did it with kindness, grace and that famous wit and smile. It’s been hard to not be in tears all day. There will never be another Dolly Parton.”

 Jason Kempin / Getty Images

 Sharing a photo of himself and Dolly on The Voice, Blake Shelton wrote, “I can say with absolute certainty that we are all feeling the same heart brokenness today. I only got to spend any real time with Dolly when Gwen [Stefani] and I got to work with her on The Voice. I want everyone to know that she was the EXACT person that you think she is. It was like being with the funnest, most loving, most caring and closest member of your family. Truly a loss for the entire world. We love you Dolly.”

 View this photo on Instagram

 @blakeshelton / Trae Patton / NBCU Photo Bank / NBCUniversal via Getty Images via Getty Images

 Zac Brown shared on Instagram, “She was a real angel long before now. Her faith was number one. There will never be another Dolly Parton. Pure talent, pure soul, pure love. She lived by example. My wife and I are heartbroken but so blessed to know her heart. Dolly is a national treasure. She sang her heart out on Butterfly, and I will never forget the first time that I heard what she sang on it and how much she loved that song.”

 Jeff Kravitz / Getty Images

“Our hearts go out to her family, her team, and all of her friends. I believe she would want us to celebrate her life, be true to who we are, and show each other love and kindness. She loved Jesus and lived like He did, by example. Thank you, Dolly, for all the love and music you put into this world. You will live on in your songs and in all of our hearts,” the post added.

 Singer-songwriter Brandi Carlile shared a lengthy, heartwarming statement honoring the late star, which began, “Dolly traded in her butterfly wings today. I felt her leaving all week and I’ve been singing ‘Coat Of Many Colors’ with I’m With Her and asking folks to pray everyday. I don’t even know why. She took my face in her hands and prayed over me once. I’ve never been the same since. Her prayers were maybe more powerful than mine or anyone else’s, because that prayer has had a very long rainbow colored halo and I hope it lasts me my whole life.”

 Kevin Mazur / Getty Images

“Dolly had a way of deeply belonging to every one of us, and yet somehow still not being of this world. There’s really only one other person in human history I can think of who has held that light,” she wrote in part.“Before I met her, I loved her because she took a risk and accepted me (and all of us) for being gay in a time where she didn’t need to say anything. And she has been asked to comment and speak on MANY things over the years… choosing only to speak on that which brings love and mercy to real people, and shutting down any line of questioning that won’t. She never wavered on accepting anyone for who they were and who they were meant to be,” she said. “After I met her, I loved her for being obscenely generous, whip smart and possessing the kind of otherworldly discernment I’ll never stop chasing.”Brandi added, “And yet I’m nobody and everyone all at once. Just a heartbroken Dolly fan at the end of the day with a head full of memories, prayers and songs left behind by a big breasted angel with a twinkle in her eye and the whole world in her hands.”

 Colman Domingo said, “Dolly taught us that you can be anything and do anything and to do it with kindness. What a light. We are all grateful that we lived in a time of Dolly Parton. We will always love her.”

 Araya Doheny / Getty Images

 Kevin Costner, who personally sought Dolly’s permission to use her 1973 song “I Will Always Love You” in the 1992 film The Bodyguard, wrote on Instagram, “Oh my goodness! Where did you go Dolly? We are all breathless. The feeling of who you are and who you were are so close,” he wrote. “We have all stopped for a moment to think of the miracle that was you. Thank you for trusting me with ‘I Will Always Love You.’ So gracious in all things. We are all at a loss this moment. Forgive us but we will miss you so much. So much.”

 ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection

 Retired musician Linda Ronstadt made a rare public statement to honor Dolly’s passing. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my friend, Dolly Parton. One of the most extraordinary musical experiences of my life was recording with her. The world is a poorer place without her,” she wrote on Facebook.

 New York Daily News Archive / Getty Images

 Amazon founder and multibillionaire Jeff Bezos wrote, “Dolly spent her whole life showing us what it means to lead with love. Lauren [Sánchez Bezos] and I are so grateful to have known her. She lifted everyone with her music, her generosity, and her joy. Sending our sincere condolences to her family and everyone she touched.”

 Anadolu / Getty Images

 The CEO of Apple, Tim Cook, wrote on X, “Dolly Parton’s music helped light up the world. She was a brilliant songwriter, cultural icon, and dedicated philanthropist who helped instill a love of reading and learning in millions of children around the world. May she rest in peace.”

 @tim_cook / Via x.com

 Harvey Mason Jr., CEO of The Recording Academy, shared, “It’s nearly impossible to fully capture the depth of what Dolly Parton means to the world...Through her unwavering dedication to philanthropy, she gave back to her community and to the world with the same heart that defined her music. On behalf of the Recording Academy, our thoughts are with Dolly’s family, friends and the countless fans whose lives she touched. Her legacy – one of talent, kindness and resilience – will endure for generations to come.”

 Rebecca Sapp / Getty Images

 Bill Anderson, who bagged a Grammy nomination with Dolly in 2022 for their song “Someday It’ll All Make Sense (Bluegrass Version),” reflected on his last conversation with Dolly in a heartfelt Instagram post. “The last thing Dolly said to me was, ‘Bill Anderson – I will Always Love You,’” he recalled. “She was looking me in the eye from the giant video screen in the the Grand Ole Opry House on the occasion of my 65th Opry Anniversary a few weeks ago. She was smiling as only Dolly could, making my night even more special than it already was. The news of her passing has rocked my world, but as we sang together back in 2023, ‘Someday It’ll All Make Sense.’”

 Tony R. Phipps / Getty Images

 SAG-AFTRA president Sean Astin said in part, “The passing of Dolly Parton will be deeply felt throughout our membership. Her life and legacy of joy and creativity had an indescribable impact on the world. As a singer, songwriter, performer, business leader and all-around visionary, Dolly Parton’s talent is revered across generations. Her basic humanity is known to the world and she is simply beloved by countless millions. Personally, from 9 to 5 when she effortlessly advanced the cause of professional women, to her Islands in the Stream collaboration with Kenny Rogers, I’m a true and forever fan. On behalf of SAG-AFTRA and my family, we send thoughts of love and condolences to her family.”

 Terry Wyatt / Getty Images

 Keke Palmer wrote, “I’m devastated. Truly.”

 @keke / Via instagram.com

 John Stamos said, “Shine on, Dolly. We will miss you.”

 NBC / Getty Images

 Rosie O’Donnell wrote, “This earth angel has gone back to heaven where she came from - heartbroken 💔 #iwillalwaysloveyou”

 Randy Holmes / Getty Images

 Kyle Richards said, “Thank you for all the joy you brought to so many 🙏 Rest in Peace 🤍 💔”

 Cindy Ord / Getty Images

 Paris Hilton was one of several celebs who paid tribute to Dolly directly under the late star’s Instagram page. “Forever my icon 👸🏼💫 You will be missed🥹,” she wrote.

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Olivia Munn wrote, "I will always love you ❤️❤️❤️❤️"

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Luke Evans commented, “Rest in plush cotton dear Dolly we will always love you ❤️” — a reference to Dolly’s nephew’s revelation that her final wish was to be laid to rest in a “beautiful bed of plush cotton.”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Sophia Bush wrote, “This one cuts deep. What an icon. What a humanitarian. What A GAL. We love you, Dolly.”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Kelsea Ballerini commented, “one of one. thank you dolly. 🦋”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Donatella Versace wrote, “We’ll never forget you, Dolly 🤍,” and, "An icon. She will be missed 🤍🕊️"

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Our thoughts are with Dolly’s family and loved ones.

This post is being updated.

news.title: Celebrities React To Dolly Parton's Death
news.text:
On Aug. 25, news broke that beloved country music icon and philanthropist Dolly Parton had sadly died at age 80.

 NBC / Getty Images

 Dolly’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, made the announcement in a video shared to Instagram on behalf of the Parton family. “This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality,” he said. “As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment, but haven't truly felt it until now.”

 Silver Screen Collection / Getty Images

“Dolly opened doors not just for me, but for her entire family to reach the potential we didn't even know was possible,” Bryan added in part. “Dolly also opened doors for generations of singers, songwriters, musicians, and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent. By her example, we believed that anything was possible. She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the doors she opened made and changed history.”

 The news of Dolly’s death comes just days after the star issued an update on her health issues, which she began to publicly address after the death of her husband, Carl Dean, in March 2025.

 View this photo on Instagram

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

“As I’ve shared in video messages throughout the past year, I am dealing with some health issues that I just didn’t pay attention to when I was watching over Carl,” she told People on Aug. 21. “Even though I’m still healin’, I’m still workin’! You know me — as I’ve often said — I’ve dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I’m gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life.”

 In the wake of the heartbreaking news, here’s how celebrities across the globe are mourning Dolly’s passing:

“Our hearts go out to her family, her team, and all of her friends. I believe she would want us to celebrate her life, be true to who we are, and show each other love and kindness. She loved Jesus and lived like He did, by example. Thank you, Dolly, for all the love and music you put into this world. You will live on in your songs and in all of our hearts,” the post added.

 Singer-songwriter Brandi Carlile shared a lengthy, heartwarming statement honoring the late star, which began, “Dolly traded in her butterfly wings today. I felt her leaving all week and I’ve been singing ‘Coat Of Many Colors’ with I’m With Her and asking folks to pray everyday. I don’t even know why. She took my face in her hands and prayed over me once. I’ve never been the same since. Her prayers were maybe more powerful than mine or anyone else’s, because that prayer has had a very long rainbow colored halo and I hope it lasts me my whole life.”

 Kevin Mazur / Getty Images

“Dolly had a way of deeply belonging to every one of us, and yet somehow still not being of this world. There’s really only one other person in human history I can think of who has held that light,” she wrote in part.“Before I met her, I loved her because she took a risk and accepted me (and all of us) for being gay in a time where she didn’t need to say anything. And she has been asked to comment and speak on MANY things over the years… choosing only to speak on that which brings love and mercy to real people, and shutting down any line of questioning that won’t. She never wavered on accepting anyone for who they were and who they were meant to be,” she said. “After I met her, I loved her for being obscenely generous, whip smart and possessing the kind of otherworldly discernment I’ll never stop chasing.”Brandi added, “And yet I’m nobody and everyone all at once. Just a heartbroken Dolly fan at the end of the day with a head full of memories, prayers and songs left behind by a big breasted angel with a twinkle in her eye and the whole world in her hands.”

 Colman Domingo said, “Dolly taught us that you can be anything and do anything and to do it with kindness. What a light. We are all grateful that we lived in a time of Dolly Parton. We will always love her.”

 Araya Doheny / Getty Images

 Kevin Costner, who personally sought Dolly’s permission to use her 1973 song “I Will Always Love You” in the 1992 film The Bodyguard, wrote on Instagram, “Oh my goodness! Where did you go Dolly? We are all breathless. The feeling of who you are and who you were are so close,” he wrote. “We have all stopped for a moment to think of the miracle that was you. Thank you for trusting me with ‘I Will Always Love You.’ So gracious in all things. We are all at a loss this moment. Forgive us but we will miss you so much. So much.”

 ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection

 Retired musician Linda Ronstadt made a rare public statement to honor Dolly’s passing. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my friend, Dolly Parton. One of the most extraordinary musical experiences of my life was recording with her. The world is a poorer place without her,” she wrote on Facebook.

 New York Daily News Archive / Getty Images

 Amazon founder and multibillionaire Jeff Bezos wrote, “Dolly spent her whole life showing us what it means to lead with love. Lauren [Sánchez Bezos] and I are so grateful to have known her. She lifted everyone with her music, her generosity, and her joy. Sending our sincere condolences to her family and everyone she touched.”

 Anadolu / Getty Images

 The CEO of Apple, Tim Cook, wrote on X, “Dolly Parton’s music helped light up the world. She was a brilliant songwriter, cultural icon, and dedicated philanthropist who helped instill a love of reading and learning in millions of children around the world. May she rest in peace.”

 @tim_cook / Via x.com

 Harvey Mason Jr., CEO of The Recording Academy, shared, “It’s nearly impossible to fully capture the depth of what Dolly Parton means to the world...Through her unwavering dedication to philanthropy, she gave back to her community and to the world with the same heart that defined her music. On behalf of the Recording Academy, our thoughts are with Dolly’s family, friends and the countless fans whose lives she touched. Her legacy – one of talent, kindness and resilience – will endure for generations to come.”

 Rebecca Sapp / Getty Images

 Bill Anderson, who bagged a Grammy nomination with Dolly in 2022 for their song “Someday It’ll All Make Sense (Bluegrass Version),” reflected on his last conversation with Dolly in a heartfelt Instagram post. “The last thing Dolly said to me was, ‘Bill Anderson – I will Always Love You,’” he recalled. “She was looking me in the eye from the giant video screen in the the Grand Ole Opry House on the occasion of my 65th Opry Anniversary a few weeks ago. She was smiling as only Dolly could, making my night even more special than it already was. The news of her passing has rocked my world, but as we sang together back in 2023, ‘Someday It’ll All Make Sense.’”

 Tony R. Phipps / Getty Images

 SAG-AFTRA president Sean Astin said in part, “The passing of Dolly Parton will be deeply felt throughout our membership. Her life and legacy of joy and creativity had an indescribable impact on the world. As a singer, songwriter, performer, business leader and all-around visionary, Dolly Parton’s talent is revered across generations. Her basic humanity is known to the world and she is simply beloved by countless millions. Personally, from 9 to 5 when she effortlessly advanced the cause of professional women, to her Islands in the Stream collaboration with Kenny Rogers, I’m a true and forever fan. On behalf of SAG-AFTRA and my family, we send thoughts of love and condolences to her family.”

 Terry Wyatt / Getty Images

 Keke Palmer wrote, “I’m devastated. Truly.”

 @keke / Via instagram.com

 John Stamos said, “Shine on, Dolly. We will miss you.”

 NBC / Getty Images

 Rosie O’Donnell wrote, “This earth angel has gone back to heaven where she came from - heartbroken 💔 #iwillalwaysloveyou”

 Randy Holmes / Getty Images

 Kyle Richards said, “Thank you for all the joy you brought to so many 🙏 Rest in Peace 🤍 💔”

 Cindy Ord / Getty Images

 Paris Hilton was one of several celebs who paid tribute to Dolly directly under the late star’s Instagram page. “Forever my icon 👸🏼💫 You will be missed🥹,” she wrote.

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Olivia Munn wrote, "I will always love you ❤️❤️❤️❤️"

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Luke Evans commented, “Rest in plush cotton dear Dolly we will always love you ❤️” — a reference to Dolly’s nephew’s revelation that her final wish was to be laid to rest in a “beautiful bed of plush cotton.”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Sophia Bush wrote, “This one cuts deep. What an icon. What a humanitarian. What A GAL. We love you, Dolly.”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Kelsea Ballerini commented, “one of one. thank you dolly. 🦋”

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Donatella Versace wrote, “We’ll never forget you, Dolly 🤍,” and, "An icon. She will be missed 🤍🕊️"

 @dollyparton / Via instagram.com

 Our thoughts are with Dolly’s family and loved ones.

news.title: US midterm elections: Democrats gain ground as Trump faces growing voter discontent
news.text:
The official campaign for the US midterm elections usually begins after America celebrates Labor Day on September 7. But over the summer, the battle for votes has intensified between Donald Trump’s Republican party and a freshly emboldened Democratic party. 

In November’s elections, all the seats in the House of Representatives will be contested, as will one-third of the Senate. Throughout the year, Republican and Democratic hopefuls have been engaged in the primary election process. 

These are now nearing a conclusion. Primaries have now been held across the country for gubernatorial, Senate and House contests. Following the August 18 primaries, polling showed the Democrats with a six-point lead. 

The Democratic party has also been buoyed by data from earlier in the month from a Reuters/Ipsos poll that revealed for the first time in nearly a decade that voters prefer the party’s approach to the economy. This could be a decisive factor come election day on November 3. 

Elaine Kamarck, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, a thinktank, has asserted that in America’s current bitterly divided political climate “where more congressional districts than ever before are considered ‘safe’ for one party or the other, real change plays out in congressional primaries”.

Results from the August 18 primaries in Florida, Alaska and Wyoming have underlined the current shifts in voting preferences among both Republican and Democratic supporters. 

On the Democrat side, there appears to be a developing trend of candidates on the party’s left defeating centrist hopefuls. In Florida, democratic socialist Angie Nixon defeated her moderate Democrat opponent, Alex Vindman. 

The result was striking for two reasons. First, the contrast in campaign spending by both candidates. Nixon raised US$975,000 (£716,000) compared to Vindman’s war chest of over US$16.3 million. 

The other noteworthy point was Nixon’s robust position on Israel. She advocated stripping the country of US aid, something that is politically risky in a state that contains America’s third-largest Jewish population. 

This was by no means uniform – other candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) lost out to more established Democratic candidates. But Nixon’s victory represented another progressive outsider advancing to November’s elections – something already witnessed in states like Wisconsin, Minnesota and Michigan. 

DSA figures have been able to tap into significant frustration among the Democratic voter base that has become increasingly vexed by cost-of-living issues as well as growing discontent towards their party establishment. 

Trump ticket no longer golden

Democrats are now beginning to feel increasingly optimistic about their chances to take back control of the US Senate after November. This would require a net gain of four seats. 

An emerging trend from recent Republican results suggests that the once hugely sought-after Trump endorsement is no longer the guarantee of victory it once was. The president’s first choice in Florida’s 19th congressional district, Catalina Lauf, lost out to Jim Schwartzel. Similarly, in Wyoming’s Republican primary for governor the sitting state senator Eric Barlow defeated the Trump-backed candidate Megan Degenfelder. 

In South Carolina, Darline Graham – who replaced her brother Lindsay Graham as senator when he died in July – won a run-off primary with the strong backing of the president. But given the late Senator Graham’s prominent profile, she is perhaps best seen as a continuity candidate, winning on name recognition as much as on the Trump endorsement. 

This apparent defiance against the 47th president among registered Republican voters seems to be increasingly common, with the president’s preferences in Iowa, Georgia and South Carolina’s gubernatorial races all losing. 

Trump’s job approval ratings remain in negative territory. A recent RealClearPolitics polling average had the president’s approval rating at 39.2% with 58.4% of respondents saying they disapprove of his performance. 

The war in Iran is having a daily impact on the lives of ordinary Americans through rising fuel prices. The survey also revealed that just three out of ten voters approved of Trump’s management of the conflict. This may explain why some Republican voters are prepared to reject the president’s endorsement.

Rural voters

Rural voters are emerging as a key demographic that appears to be turning away from Trump. Sharp rises in fuel and fertiliser costs are hitting grain producers particularly hard, while Trump’s tariff regime is hurting agricultural exports.

A recent Fox News analysis found that among rural voters, Trump’s net job approval fell from +20 in early 2025 to -14 in May 2026. A recent article by Brookings senior fellow, William A. Galston, pointed to the fact that Trump carried 64% of the rural vote to Kamala Harris’s 34% in 2024. He believes that in November, while Republican voters may not choose to cast their ballot for Democratic candidates, there’s a strong possibility more will choose not to vote at all.

There was further bad news for the Republicans in a Pew Research study from July which found that, despite Trump himself not being on the ballot, nearly twice as many voters – 42% – will use their ballot to vote against him as those who will use it to vote for him.

But all might not be lost just yet for the GOP. It may look as if the Democrats are on course to retake the House of Representatives – and potentially also the Senate – in November. But we have yet to discover the impact of significant redistricting by various states under the administration of both parties.

Redistricting is when a state redraws the boundaries of its electoral seats to better reflect the state’s demographics. This happens automatically every ten years. But a number of states have redrawn their boundaries since July 2025 outside this automatic process. Analysis shows that out of the ten states to have engaged in a voluntary redistricting process, the new electoral maps of eight favour Republicans. 

So while Democrats have a clear polling edge and obvious momentum, the results of the midterms are still far from certain.
news.summary: Trump-endorsed candidates are performing badly in primary ballots.

news.title: GOP’s ‘Decoy Dan’ Sullivan Advances in Arkansas as Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan Also Moves On
news.text:
WASHINGTON — A Republican candidate in Alaska who shares a name with the state’s incumbent senator, Dan Sullivan, moved through the open primary Wednesday, adding fresh confusion to a GOP race that Democrats hope could work in their favor.

Retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan secured a spot in Alaska’s open primary system, which advances the top four finishers regardless of party to the general election, according to multiple projections issued more than a week after the Aug. 18 vote.

The candidate, nicknamed “Decoy Dan” after registering as a Republican just days before the primary, will appear in the final stretch alongside GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and Democratic former Rep. Peltola.

The identity of the fourth candidate headed to the November ballot was not immediately clear.

Alaska will use ranked-choice voting in the general election.

Peltola has been ahead in polling in the closely watched Alaska Senate race, even though the state has traditionally leaned Republican.

Dan J. Sullivan has rejected claims that he is a Democratic plant whose matching name could peel votes away from Sen. Sullivan and indirectly help Peltola.

He has described himself as a moderate Republican, though he told the New York Times he voted for the Democratic presidential nominee in each of the last three elections, attended at least one “No Kings” protest and supported Peltola in both of her congressional campaigns.

The Last Frontier state last picked a Democrat for Senate in 2008, but Peltola managed to flip Alaska’s at-large US House seat in 2022, proving that she is a force to be reckoned with in statewide races.

Democrats see Alaska as one of their top four pick-up opportunities for the Senate this cycle alongside Maine, Ohio and North Carolina.

Complicating things for the Republicans has been Dan J. Sullivan’s inclusion on the ballot.

While a lower court judge initially kicked him off the ballot, citing evidence that he wasn’t mounting “an actual good-faith candidacy,” the Alaska Supreme Court let him back on.

The lower court judge had knocked “Decoy Dan” for registering as a Republican days before filing his candidacy.

Peltola’s campaign has meanwhile been hit by recent turbulence.

Earlier this month, Peltola ignited controversy when her campaign said it didn’t approve of former Vice President Kamala Harris’ fundraising message in support of her Senate bid.

Harris had urged her supporters to back Peltola, who is trying to win in a state that the former veep lost by about 14 percentage points.

Afterward, Peltola lost several senior campaign officials in what her team described as a shake-up to prepare for the general election.

She has been trying to run as a centrist-type Democrat in her effort to appeal to Alaska’s famously maverick voters.

Peltola has a 2-percentage-point edge over Sen. Sullivan in the latest RealClearPolitics aggregate of polls in a hypothetical two-way matchup.
